source.text: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ κύριος καὶ ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα δύο καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: After now these things appointed the Lord also others seventy-two and sent them two [by] two before [the] face of him into every town and place where was about he himself to come.

en.L: Now after these things the Lord appointed seventy-two others also, and sent them two by two ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into every town and place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} was about to come.
en.B: After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others as well. He sent them out in pairs ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to every town and place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going to visit.
en.R: After this, the Lord chose seventy-two more of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He sent them out two at a time to go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were to go to every town and place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned to go.

es.L: Y después de estas cosas designó el Señor también a otros setenta y dos, y los envió de dos en dos delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a toda ciudad y lugar adonde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo iba a ir.
es.B: Después de esto, el Señor designó a otros setenta y dos. Los envió de dos en dos delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, a todos los pueblos y lugares que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pensaba visitar.
es.R: Después de esto, el Señor escogió a otros setenta y dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Los envió de dos en dos para que fueran delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Tenían que ir a cada pueblo y lugar adonde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pensaba ir.

fr.L: Après cela, le Seigneur désigna aussi soixante-douze autres, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les envoya deux par deux en avant de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans toute ville et [tout] lieu où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} devait {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} aller.
fr.B: Après cela, le Seigneur en désigna soixante-douze autres. Il les envoya deux à deux devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, dans toutes les villes et tous les endroits où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait se rendre.
fr.R: Ensuite, le Seigneur a choisi soixante-douze autres de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Il les a envoyés deux par deux pour qu’ils partent avant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils devaient aller dans chaque ville et chaque endroit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait l’intention d’aller.

sw.L: Basi baada ya mambo haya Bwana aliwateua wengine pia sabini na wawili, akawatuma wawili wawili mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika kila mji na mahali ambapo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alikuwa karibu kufika.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo Bwana aliwateua wengine sabini na wawili, akawatuma wawili wawili watangulie mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, waende katika kila mji na kila mahali alipokusudia kwenda.
sw.R: Baada ya hayo, Bwana aliwachagua wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wengine sabini na wawili. Aliwatuma wawili wawili wamtangulie. Walipaswa kwenda katika kila mji na kila mahali alipopanga kwenda.

vi.L: Sau những việc ấy, Chúa cũng chỉ định bảy mươi hai người khác và sai họ từng đôi một đi trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào mọi thành và mọi nơi mà chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sắp đến.
vi.B: Sau đó, Chúa chỉ định thêm bảy mươi hai người khác nữa. Ngài sai họ đi từng đôi một, đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến mọi thành và mọi nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sắp đến.
vi.R: Sau việc ấy, Chúa Giê-xu chọn thêm bảy mươi hai môn đồ khác. Ngài sai họ đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, mỗi lần hai người. Họ phải đến mọi thị trấn và mọi nơi mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} định đến.

ko.L: 이 일들 후에 주님께서 다른 일흔두 사람도 세우셔서, 그분 자신이 가시려고 하던 모든 고을과 장소로 그들을 둘씩 둘씩 그분의 얼굴 앞에 보내셨다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 주님께서 다른 일흔두 사람을 더 세우셨다. 그리고 그들을 둘씩 짝지어, 주님께서 친히 가시려던 모든 고을과 장소로 앞서 보내셨다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 주 예수께서 제자들 가운데서 일흔두 사람을 더 뽑으셨다. 그리고 그들을 두 사람씩 짝지어 먼저 보내셨다. 그들은 예수께서 가시려고 하는 모든 마을과 장소로 가야 했다.

pt.L: E, depois destas coisas, o Senhor designou também outros setenta e dois e os enviou de dois em dois adiante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, a toda cidade e lugar aonde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} mesmo estava para ir.
pt.B: Depois disso, o Senhor designou mais setenta e dois. Ele os enviou de dois em dois à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} frente, a todas as cidades e lugares que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ia visitar.
pt.R: Depois disso, o Senhor escolheu mais setenta e dois dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores. Ele os mandou de dois em dois para irem na frente {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. Eles deviam ir a todas as cidades e lugares aonde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pretendia ir.

am.L: ከዚህም በኋላ ጌታ ሌሎች ሰባ ሁለት ደግሞ ሾመ፤ እርሱ ራሱ ሊመጣበት ወዳለው ከተማና ስፍራ ሁሉ ሁለት ሁለት አድርጎ በፊቱ ላካቸው።
am.B: ከዚህ በኋላ ጌታ ሌሎች ሰባ ሁለት ሰዎችን ደግሞ ሾመ። እርሱ ሊጎበኛቸው ወዳሰባቸው ከተሞችና ስፍራዎች ሁሉ ሁለት ሁለት አድርጎ ቀድመውት እንዲሄዱ ላካቸው።
am.R: ከዚህ በኋላ ጌታ ከደቀ መዛሙርቱ መካከል ሌሎች ሰባ ሁለት ሰዎችን መረጠ። ሁለት ሁለት አድርጎ ቀድመውት እንዲሄዱ ላካቸው። እርሱ ሊሄድባቸው ወዳቀዳቸው ከተሞችና ስፍራዎች ሁሉ መሄድ ነበረባቸው።

decisions.choice: seventy-two (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The manuscripts are divided, and early ones stand on both sides. Some, among them Papyrus 75 and Codex Vaticanus, read seventy-two; others, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Alexandrinus, and most later manuscripts, read seventy. The same split comes again at 10:17. Both numbers have Old Testament echoes: the nations listed in Genesis 10 number seventy in the Hebrew text and seventy-two in the Greek Old Testament, and Moses chose seventy elders, with two more who also prophesied in the camp (Numbers 11:16-26). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: others also: more messengers, besides the Twelve sent out in 9:1-6
alternatives: others besides the messengers sent ahead in 9:52
decisions.reason: Jesus gave the Twelve much the same instructions in 9:1-5. He also sent messengers ahead of him in 9:52, and the wording may include them. Either way, the mission now widens beyond the Twelve.

decisions.choice: before his face: ahead of him, to prepare for his coming
decisions.reason: The phrase is a Hebrew way of saying "ahead of". It was used of the messengers in 9:52 and of the messenger God sends ahead in Malachi 3:1 (Luke 7:27). The seventy-two go to the places Jesus himself will visit.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: Luke the narrator often calls Jesus "the Lord" (7:13, 19; 10:39, 41).

decisions.choice: more of his followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who the others were: they were disciples of Jesus (10:23).

decisions.choice: chose
decisions.reason: The verb means to name someone publicly for a task. Readable uses a common word.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (él, sus, lo, te, mí)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("designó", "envió") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("pídanle"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: discípulos
decisions.reason: The English Readable supplies "followers" to say who the seventy-two were (rendering decision r-en-1). The New Testament drafts use "discípulos" at every level for Jesus's followers, so Readable supplies that word here and in 10:17.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R) (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, and the story Jesus tells in 10:30-35 is in the passé composé (style guide section 9).

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in Mark and Colossians. French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for Jesus carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and so do pronouns French needs where English has none. A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital ("Il les envoya").

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yake, yeye, mwenyewe, wake)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili carries most pronouns in the verb ("akawatuma", "wamtangulie"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Matthew. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi
decisions.reason: The English Readable supplies "followers" to say who the seventy-two were (rendering decision r-en-1). The New Testament drafts use "wanafunzi" at every level for Jesus's followers, so Readable supplies that word here and in 10:17.

decisions.choice: "Chúa" (L, B); "Chúa Giê-xu" (R) for the narrator's "the Lord" (also 10:39, 10:41)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 7:13: the narrator gives Jesus the title used for God (meaning decision), and Readable adds the name, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "môn đồ" (R) where the English Readable says "followers"
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "môn đồ" at every level. "Ngài" for Jesus in the narrative and "Ta" when he speaks, as in Luke 4-9.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Luke 10; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in 해라체, people speak to him in 합쇼체, and he prays to the Father in 합쇼체
alternatives: Korean spans for pronouns referring to Jesus or God
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (Korean style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "주님께서" (L, B), "주 예수께서" (R) for Luke's narrative "the Lord"; "일흔두 사람"
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 7:13. The number is written in Korean words, as the style guide asks for short numbers.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
alternatives: Marking pronouns for God and Jesus
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus has nothing to change in Amharic. The pronouns ("እርሱ", "በፊቱ") stand plain in every level of this passage.

source.text: ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι· δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐργάτας ἐκβάλῃ εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He was saying then to them, The indeed harvest [is] plentiful, but the workers few; ask therefore the Lord of the harvest that workers he may send out into the harvest of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "The harvest [is] plentiful, but the workers [are] few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} send out workers into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest.
en.B: He told them, "There is a great harvest, but only a few workers. So plead with the Lord of the harvest to send workers out to bring in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest.
en.R: Jesus told them, "There is a big harvest to gather, but there are only a few workers. So pray to the Lord who owns the harvest. Ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to send out more workers to bring in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest.

es.L: Y les decía: «La cosecha [es] abundante, pero los trabajadores [son] pocos; {{plural_you:rueguen|rogad}}, pues, al Señor de la cosecha que envíe trabajadores a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cosecha.
es.B: Les dijo: «Hay una gran cosecha, pero solo unos pocos trabajadores. Por eso, {{plural_you:pídanle|pedidle}} al Señor de la cosecha que mande trabajadores a recoger {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cosecha.
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Hay mucha cosecha para recoger, pero hay pocos trabajadores. Por eso, {{plural_you:oren|orad}} al Señor, que es el dueño de la cosecha. {{plural_you:Pídanle|Pedidle}} que envíe más trabajadores para recoger {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cosecha.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait : « La moisson [est] abondante, mais les ouvriers [sont] peu nombreux. Priez donc le Seigneur de la moisson pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} envoie des ouvriers dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} moisson.
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Il y a beaucoup à moissonner, mais les ouvriers sont peu nombreux. Suppliez donc le Seigneur de la moisson d’envoyer des ouvriers pour rentrer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} moisson.
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Il y a une grande récolte à rentrer, mais il n’y a que peu d’ouvriers. Alors priez le Seigneur à qui appartient la récolte. Demandez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} d’envoyer d’autres ouvriers pour rentrer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} récolte.

sw.L: Alikuwa akiwaambia, "Mavuno [ni] mengi, lakini wafanyakazi [ni] wachache. Kwa hiyo msihini Bwana wa mavuno, ili awatume wafanyakazi waende kwenye mavuno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Mavuno ni makubwa, lakini wafanyakazi ni wachache tu. Kwa hiyo mwombeni kwa bidii Bwana wa mavuno, awapeleke wafanyakazi wakavune mavuno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Kuna mavuno mengi ya kukusanya, lakini wafanyakazi ni wachache tu. Kwa hiyo mwombeni Bwana ambaye ni mwenye mavuno. Mwombeni awatume wafanyakazi zaidi wakavune mavuno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Mùa gặt thì nhiều, nhưng thợ gặt thì ít; vậy hãy cầu xin Chủ của mùa gặt sai thợ gặt vào mùa gặt của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ngài bảo họ: "Mùa gặt thật lớn, nhưng thợ gặt lại ít. Vậy các con hãy nài xin Chủ mùa gặt sai thợ gặt đến gặt mùa màng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Mùa lúa chín chờ gặt thì rất nhiều, nhưng thợ gặt thì ít. Vậy các con hãy cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng làm chủ mùa gặt. Hãy xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sai thêm thợ gặt đến gặt mùa màng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하고 계셨다. "추수할 것은 많은데 일꾼은 적다. 그러므로 추수의 주인께 그분의 추수 [밭]으로 일꾼들을 보내 주시라고 간청하여라.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "거둘 곡식은 많은데 일꾼은 적다. 그러니 추수의 주인께 일꾼들을 보내셔서 곡식을 거두어들이게 해 달라고 간청하여라.
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "거두어들일 곡식은 많은데 일할 사람은 적다. 그러니 추수할 밭의 주인이신 하나님께 기도하여라. 일꾼들을 더 보내셔서 곡식을 거두어들이게 해 달라고 하여라.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes dizia: "A colheita [é] grande, mas os trabalhadores [são] poucos; peçam, portanto, ao Senhor da colheita que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} envie trabalhadores para a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} colheita.
pt.B: Ele lhes disse: "A colheita é grande, mas os trabalhadores são poucos. Por isso, supliquem ao Senhor da colheita que mande trabalhadores para recolher a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} colheita.
pt.R: Jesus disse a eles: "Há uma grande colheita para recolher, mas os trabalhadores são poucos. Por isso, orem ao Senhor, que é o dono da colheita. Peçam a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} que mande mais trabalhadores para recolher a colheita {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

am.L: እንዲህም ይላቸው ነበር፦ «መከሩ ብዙ [ነው]፤ ሠራተኞቹ ግን ጥቂቶች [ናቸው]፤ ስለዚህ የመከሩ ጌታ ሠራተኞችን ወደ መከሩ እንዲልክ ለምኑት።
am.B: እንዲህም አላቸው፦ «አዝመራው ብዙ ነው፤ ሠራተኞቹ ግን ጥቂት ናቸው። ስለዚህ ወደ አዝመራው ጌታ ጸልዩ፤ አዝመራውን የሚሰበስቡ ሠራተኞችን እንዲልክ ለምኑት።
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «የሚሰበሰብ ብዙ አዝመራ አለ፤ ሠራተኞቹ ግን ጥቂት ብቻ ናቸው። ስለዚህ የአዝመራው ባለቤት ወደ ሆነው ጌታ ጸልዩ። አዝመራውን የሚሰበስቡ ተጨማሪ ሠራተኞች እንዲልክ ለምኑት።

decisions.choice: the harvest is plentiful: many people are ready to be gathered in for the kingdom of God
decisions.reason: The harvest is a picture of people being gathered in, as in John 4:35-38. Elsewhere a harvest can picture judgment (Joel 3:13), but here the workers gather people who will receive the message.

decisions.choice: the Lord of the harvest: God, who owns the harvest and sends its workers
decisions.reason: The owner of a harvest decides who works in it. The disciples are to ask him for workers. Yet Jesus is the one who sends the seventy-two (10:1, 3); God's work and his are one (10:16).

decisions.choice: send out: send with urgency, thrust out
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for driving out demons (9:40). Used of workers it stresses urgency: the harvest will not wait.

decisions.choice: ask: plead, pray
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask earnestly for something one needs. Luke uses it for prayer (5:12; 21:36).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker at the start of the speech.

decisions.choice: the Lord who owns the harvest
decisions.reason: Readable says what "Lord of the harvest" means.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every verb and pronoun addressed to the seventy-two; the « opens here and stays open to the end of 10:16
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them, and English has no such choice. Jesus speaks from here to 10:16, so the words he gives them to say take “ ”, as the English puts them in single marks.

decisions.choice: cosecha, trabajadores
decisions.reason: The words used across the New Testament drafts. "Mies" and "obreros" are the traditional church words; "cosecha" and "trabajadores" are the everyday ones and keep the picture of a farm at harvest time (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: msihini (L); mwombeni kwa bidii (B); mwombeni (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to plead or pray (meaning decision m4). Literal uses "kusihi", to beg earnestly; Balanced adds "kwa bidii" to the everyday "kuomba", and Readable keeps the plain word. Jesus speaks from here to 10:16, so the quotation stays open, and the words he gives them to say take single marks.

decisions.choice: "Chủ của mùa gặt" (L); "Chủ mùa gặt" (B); "Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng làm chủ mùa gặt" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Matthew 9:38: the Lord of the harvest is God, the owner (meaning decision); "Chủ" says owner and master, capitalised because God is meant, and "Chúa" would sound like a title of Jesus.

decisions.choice: "các con" for the seventy-two (10:2-16, 10:18-20)
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to his disciples.

decisions.choice: "추수의 주인" (L, B); "추수할 밭의 주인이신 하나님" (R)
decisions.reason: "주인" with the honorific "께" and -시- says the owner of the harvest without making the saying sound like an address; the meaning decision identifies him as God, which Readable says.

decisions.choice: A colheita é grande, mas os trabalhadores são poucos
decisions.reason: The same saying as Matthew 9:37, in the same words. "Colheita" is the everyday word; "messe" is literary and unknown to many readers.

decisions.choice: "መከር" (harvest) at Literal; "አዝመራ" (crop, harvest field) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 9:37-38, where the Greek is the same: "መከር" is the harvest and the season of reaping; "አዝመራ" is the everyday word for a crop ready to be gathered, which reads more naturally beside "ሠራተኞች" (workers).

source.text: ὑπάγετε· ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς ἄρνας ἐν μέσῳ λύκων.

records.literal_gloss: Go; behold I send out you as lambs in [the] midst of wolves.

en.L: Go; look, I am sending you out as lambs in [the] midst of wolves.
en.B: Go on your way. I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
en.R: Go now. I am sending you out like little lambs into a pack of wolves.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}; {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envío como corderos en medio de lobos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Pónganse|Poneos}} en camino. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envío como corderos entre lobos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} ahora. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envío como corderitos en medio de una manada de lobos.

fr.L: Allez ; voici, je vous envoie comme des agneaux au milieu de loups.
fr.B: Allez. Je vous envoie comme des agneaux parmi des loups.
fr.R: Partez maintenant. Je vous envoie comme de petits agneaux au milieu d’une bande de loups.

sw.L: Nendeni; tazameni, ninawapeleka kama kondoo wachanga katikati ya mbwa mwitu.
sw.B: Nendeni zenu. Ninawatuma kama kondoo wachanga kati ya mbwa mwitu.
sw.R: Nendeni sasa. Ninawatuma kama kondoo wadogo wanaoingia katikati ya kundi la mbwa mwitu.

vi.L: Hãy đi; kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai các con đi như chiên con giữa bầy sói.
vi.B: Hãy lên đường. Ta sai các con đi như chiên con vào giữa bầy sói.
vi.R: Bây giờ hãy đi đi. Ta sai các con đi như những chú chiên con nhỏ vào giữa một bầy sói.

ko.L: 가거라. 보라, 내가 너희를 이리들 가운데로 어린양들처럼 보낸다.
ko.B: 가거라. 내가 너희를 보내는 것이 마치 어린양들을 이리 떼 가운데로 보내는 것과 같다.
ko.R: 이제 가거라. 내가 너희를 보내는 것은 어린양들을 늑대 떼 속으로 보내는 것과 같다.

pt.L: Vão; eis que eu envio vocês como cordeiros no meio de lobos.
pt.B: Vão! Estou enviando vocês como cordeiros no meio de lobos.
pt.R: Vão agora. Estou mandando vocês como cordeirinhos para o meio de uma alcateia de lobos.

am.L: ሂዱ፤ እነሆ፣ እንደ ጠቦቶች በተኩላዎች መካከል እልካችኋለሁ።
am.B: ሂዱ። እንደ ጠቦቶች በተኩላዎች መካከል እልካችኋለሁ።
am.R: አሁን ሂዱ። በተኩላዎች መንጋ መካከል እንዳሉ ትንንሽ ጠቦቶች አድርጌ እልካችኋለሁ።

decisions.choice: like lambs among wolves: without defense among people who may attack them
alternatives: among enemies who will all attack them
decisions.reason: Lambs cannot protect themselves from wolves. The messengers will go unarmed and without supplies (10:4) among people who may turn against them (10:10). Wolves are a picture of violent rulers in Ezekiel 22:27.

decisions.choice: I am sending: Jesus himself sends them as his messengers
decisions.reason: The verb is the one from which "apostle" comes. Those who hear them will be hearing Jesus (10:16).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: miren | mirad
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the Greek "look" is "mira" at Literal. Here Jesus speaks to the seventy-two, and Spanish addresses a group in the plural; Balanced and Readable leave it out, as the English does.

decisions.choice: voici (L)
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "look" because "behold" is old-fashioned. French "voici" is still current and is the natural way to point to what follows, so Literal keeps it here and in 10:19 and 10:25; Balanced and Readable carry the force in the sentence, as in English.

decisions.choice: tazameni
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the seventy-two, so Literal uses the plural command; Balanced and Readable leave the word out, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "chiên con" for lambs; "kìa" (L) for "look"
decisions.reason: Luke's word is "lambs", where Matthew 10:16 has "sheep"; "chiên con" keeps the more defenseless picture (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "어린양" for arnas; "이리" (L, B), "늑대" (R)
decisions.reason: Luke has the word for lambs, not sheep (Matthew 10:16 has sheep); the wolves are named as in the Korean Matthew 10:16.

decisions.choice: eis que
decisions.reason: As in Matthew: Literal keeps "eis que", the Portuguese word for pointing to what follows; Balanced and Readable carry its force in the sentence, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ጠቦቶች" (lambs)
decisions.reason: Luke's word is lambs, not the sheep of Matthew 10:16, so the Amharic differs from the Matthew parallel here: young animals among wolves are even more defenseless.

source.text: μὴ βαστάζετε βαλλάντιον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ ὑποδήματα, καὶ μηδένα κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἀσπάσησθε.

records.literal_gloss: Not carry purse, nor bag, nor sandals, and no one along the road greet.

en.L: Do not carry a purse, nor a bag, nor sandals, and greet no one along the road.
en.B: Take no money bag, no pack and no sandals, and do not stop to greet anyone on the way.
en.R: Do not carry a money bag, a traveler's bag, or sandals. Do not stop to talk with people along the road.

es.L: No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} bolsa, ni alforja, ni sandalias, y a nadie {{plural_you:saluden|saludéis}} por el camino.
es.B: No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} bolsa de dinero, ni morral, ni sandalias, y no {{plural_you:se detengan|os detengáis}} a saludar a nadie en el camino.
es.R: No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} bolsa para el dinero, ni bolsa de viaje, ni sandalias. No {{plural_you:se detengan|os detengáis}} a hablar con la gente por el camino.

fr.L: Ne portez ni bourse, ni sac, ni sandales, et ne saluez personne en chemin.
fr.B: N’emportez ni bourse, ni sac, ni sandales, et ne vous arrêtez pour saluer personne en chemin.
fr.R: Ne prenez pas de porte-monnaie, ni de sac de voyage, ni de sandales. Ne vous arrêtez pas pour discuter avec les gens sur la route.

sw.L: Msichukue mfuko wa fedha, wala mkoba, wala viatu, wala msimsalimu mtu yeyote njiani.
sw.B: Msibebe mfuko wa pesa, wala mkoba, wala viatu; na msisimame njiani kumsalimu mtu yeyote.
sw.R: Msibebe mfuko wa pesa, wala mfuko wa safari, wala viatu. Msisimame njiani kuongea na watu.

vi.L: Đừng mang túi tiền, cũng đừng [mang] bao bị, đừng [mang] dép, và dọc đường đừng chào hỏi ai.
vi.B: Đừng mang túi tiền, túi hành lý hay dép, và dọc đường đừng dừng lại chào hỏi ai.
vi.R: Đừng mang túi tiền, túi xách hay dép. Dọc đường đừng dừng lại trò chuyện với ai.

ko.L: 돈주머니도, 자루도, 신발도 가지고 다니지 말고, 길에서 아무에게도 인사하지 마라.
ko.B: 돈주머니도, 여행 자루도, 신발도 가지고 가지 마라. 그리고 길에서 누구에게도 인사하느라 머뭇거리지 마라.
ko.R: 돈주머니나 가방이나 신발을 가지고 가지 마라. 길에서 사람들과 이야기하느라 멈추지 마라.

pt.L: Não levem bolsa, nem sacola, nem sandálias, e não cumprimentem ninguém pelo caminho.
pt.B: Não levem bolsa de dinheiro, nem sacola de viagem, nem sandálias, e não parem para cumprimentar ninguém pelo caminho.
pt.R: Não levem bolsa de dinheiro, nem sacola de viagem, nem sandálias. Não parem para conversar com as pessoas pela estrada.

am.L: ኮረጆ አትያዙ፣ ስልቻ አትያዙ፣ ጫማም አትያዙ፤ በመንገድም ላይ ማንንም ሰላም አትበሉ።
am.B: የገንዘብ ኮረጆ፣ ስልቻ ወይም ጫማ አትያዙ፤ በመንገድም ላይ ሰላምታ ለመለዋወጥ አትቁሙ።
am.R: የገንዘብ ኮረጆ፣ የጉዞ ስልቻ ወይም ጫማ አትያዙ። በመንገድ ላይ ከሰዎች ጋር ለመጫወት አትቁሙ።

decisions.choice: purse, bag, sandals: a money pouch, a bag for food and supplies, and footwear
decisions.reason: They are to go without the usual supplies and depend on the people who take them in, as the Twelve did (9:3). Jesus recalls this command in 22:35. The text does not say whether "sandals" means a spare pair.

decisions.choice: greet no one along the road: let nothing delay the task
decisions.reason: Greetings could be long and formal. The command stresses urgency, as when Elisha sent Gehazi ahead with orders not to greet anyone on the way (2 Kings 4:29).

decisions.choice: do not stop to greet (B); do not stop to talk with people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the reason for the command plain: they are not to be held up on the way.

decisions.choice: "túi tiền"; "bao bị" (L), "túi hành lý" (B), "túi xách" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:8 and Luke 9:3 for the traveler's bag; the purse is a money pouch (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: bolsa (de dinheiro); sacola (de viagem)
decisions.reason: Two different bags (m1): a purse for money and a bag for food and supplies. "Alforje" is a saddlebag, and "mochila" is modern; Balanced and Readable add "de dinheiro" and "de viagem" so the two are not confused.

decisions.choice: "ኮረጆ" (pouch, purse) and "ስልቻ" (traveler's bag)
decisions.reason: "ኮረጆ" is the small pouch for money; "ስልቻ" is the bag for food and supplies on a journey, the word used for the same bag in Matthew 10:10. "ቦርሳ" is a modern handbag.

source.text: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν εἰσέλθητε οἰκίαν πρῶτον λέγετε· Εἰρήνη τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Into whatever now house you might enter, first say, Peace to the house this.

en.L: And into whatever house you enter, first say, 'Peace to this house.'
en.B: Whatever house you go into, begin by saying, 'Peace be on this household.'
en.R: When you go into a home, first say, 'May there be peace in this home.'

es.L: Y en cualquier casa en que {{plural_you:entren|entréis}}, primero {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: “Paz a esta casa”.
es.B: En la casa en que {{plural_you:entren|entréis}}, {{plural_you:comiencen|comenzad}} diciendo: “Paz a esta familia”.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en una casa, primero {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: “Que haya paz en este hogar”.

fr.L: Dans quelque maison que vous entriez, dites d’abord : “Paix à cette maison.”
fr.B: Dans toute maison où vous entrerez, commencez par dire : “Paix à cette maisonnée.”
fr.R: Quand vous entrez dans une maison, dites d’abord : “Que la paix soit dans cette maison !”

sw.L: Na nyumba yoyote mtakayoingia, kwanza semeni, 'Amani kwa nyumba hii.'
sw.B: Nyumba yoyote mtakayoingia, anzeni kwa kusema, 'Amani iwe juu ya watu wa nyumba hii.'
sw.R: Mnapoingia katika nyumba, kwanza semeni, 'Amani iwe katika nyumba hii.'

vi.L: Và vào nhà nào, trước hết hãy nói: 'Bình an cho nhà này.'
vi.B: Vào nhà nào, trước hết hãy nói: 'Xin bình an ở trên gia đình này.'
vi.R: Khi các con vào một nhà, trước hết hãy nói: 'Chúc bình an cho nhà này.'

ko.L: 어느 집에 들어가든지, 먼저 '이 집에 평안이 [있기를 빕니다]' 하고 말하여라.
ko.B: 어느 집에 들어가든지, 먼저 '이 집에 평안이 있기를 빕니다' 하고 말하여라.
ko.R: 어떤 집에 들어가면, 먼저 '이 집에 평안이 있기를 빕니다' 하고 인사하여라.

pt.L: E em qualquer casa em que entrarem, digam primeiro: 'Paz a esta casa.'
pt.B: Em qualquer casa em que entrarem, comecem dizendo: 'Paz a esta família.'
pt.R: Quando entrarem numa casa, digam primeiro: 'Que haja paz neste lar.'

am.L: ወደምትገቡበትም ቤት ሁሉ አስቀድማችሁ፦ “ለዚህ ቤት ሰላም [ይሁን]” በሉ።
am.B: ወደ ማንኛውም ቤት ስትገቡ በመጀመሪያ፦ “ሰላም ለዚህ ቤተሰብ ይሁን” በሉ።
am.R: ወደ አንድ ቤት ስትገቡ በመጀመሪያ፦ “በዚህ ቤት ሰላም ይሁን” በሉ።

decisions.choice: Peace to this house: the usual greeting, here a real blessing
alternatives: a polite form of words only
decisions.reason: "Peace" was the ordinary greeting among Jews (1 Samuel 25:6). On the lips of Jesus's messengers it offers the peace that comes with the kingdom of God (1:79; 2:14).

decisions.choice: house: the household, the people who live there
decisions.reason: The blessing is for the people of the house, as 10:6 shows.

decisions.choice: May there be peace in this home
decisions.reason: Readable words the greeting as the wish it is.

decisions.choice: "bình an" at every level (10:5-6)
decisions.reason: Peace is a key term, "bình an"; here the greeting is a real blessing (meaning decision), as in Matthew 10:13. "gia đình" (B) because the house means the people in it.

decisions.choice: "평안" for eirēnē at every level, in 10:5-6
decisions.reason: "평안" is the key term for peace in the Korean John and Luke 1-8 (style guide, section 6), and of the same instruction in the Korean Matthew 10:12-13; the greeting is in 합쇼체, the polite form to a household.

decisions.choice: família
decisions.reason: The blessing is for the people who live there (m2). Balanced says "família", as the English says "household"; Literal keeps "casa", which can also mean the household.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ᾖ ἐκεῖ υἱὸς εἰρήνης, ἐπαναπαήσεται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἀνακάμψει.

records.literal_gloss: And if there is there a son of peace, will rest upon him the peace of you; but if not, upon you it will return.

en.L: And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon {{gender:that person|him}}; but if not, it will return to you.
en.B: If someone there is a person of peace, your peace will stay with {{gender:that person|him}}. If not, it will come back to you.
en.R: If someone there is ready to receive God's peace, your peace will stay with {{gender:that person|him}}. If not, your peace will come back to you.

es.L: Y si allí hay un hijo de paz, {{plural_you:la paz de ustedes|vuestra paz}} reposará {{gender:sobre esa persona|sobre él}}; y si no, volverá a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Si allí hay una persona de paz, {{plural_you:la paz de ustedes|vuestra paz}} se quedará con {{gender:esa persona|él}}. Si no, volverá a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Si alguien allí está dispuesto a recibir la paz de Dios, {{plural_you:la paz de ustedes|vuestra paz}} se quedará con {{gender:esa persona|él}}. Si no, esa paz volverá a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et s’il y a là un fils de paix, votre paix reposera sur lui ; sinon, elle reviendra sur vous.
fr.B: S’il y a là quelqu’un qui accueille la paix, votre paix restera sur lui. Sinon, elle vous reviendra.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un, dans cette maison, est prêt à recevoir la paix de Dieu, votre paix restera sur lui. Sinon, votre paix reviendra vers vous.

sw.L: Na ikiwa yupo huko mwana wa amani, amani yenu itakaa juu yake; la sivyo, itarudi kwenu.
sw.B: Kama yupo huko mtu wa amani, amani yenu itakaa naye. Kama hayupo, itawarudia ninyi.
sw.R: Kama yupo huko mtu aliye tayari kupokea amani ya Mungu, amani yenu itakaa naye. Kama hayupo, amani yenu itawarudia.

vi.L: Và nếu ở đó có con của sự bình an, thì sự bình an của các con sẽ ở trên người ấy; bằng không, thì nó sẽ trở về với các con.
vi.B: Nếu ở đó có người yêu chuộng bình an, thì sự bình an các con chúc sẽ ở lại trên người ấy. Nếu không, sự bình an ấy sẽ trở về với các con.
vi.R: Nếu ở đó có người sẵn lòng nhận sự bình an của Đức Chúa Trời, thì lời chúc bình an của các con sẽ ở lại với người ấy. Nếu không, lời chúc ấy sẽ trở về với các con.

ko.L: 그리고 거기에 평안의 아들이 있으면, 너희의 평안이 그 사람 위에 머무를 것이다. 그러나 그렇지 않으면, [그 평안이] 너희에게로 돌아올 것이다.
ko.B: 그곳에 평안을 받을 만한 사람이 있으면, 너희가 빈 평안이 그 사람에게 머무를 것이다. 그렇지 않으면 그 평안이 너희에게로 돌아올 것이다.
ko.R: 그 집에 하나님의 평안을 받아들일 사람이 있으면, 너희가 빌어 준 평안이 그 사람에게 머무를 것이다. 그런 사람이 없으면, 그 평안이 너희에게로 돌아올 것이다.

pt.L: E, se ali houver um filho da paz, a paz de vocês repousará sobre {{gender:essa pessoa|ele}}; mas, se não, ela voltará para vocês.
pt.B: Se ali houver uma pessoa de paz, a paz de vocês ficará com ela. Se não houver, a paz voltará para vocês.
pt.R: Se ali houver alguém que esteja pronto para receber a paz de Deus, a paz de vocês vai ficar com essa pessoa. Se não houver, a paz de vocês vai voltar para vocês.

am.L: በዚያም የሰላም ልጅ ቢኖር ሰላማችሁ በእርሱ ላይ ያርፋል፤ ባይኖር ግን ወደ እናንተ ይመለሳል።
am.B: በዚያ የሰላም ሰው ቢኖር ሰላማችሁ ከእርሱ ጋር ይኖራል፤ ባይኖር ግን ወደ እናንተ ይመለሳል።
am.R: በዚያ የእግዚአብሔርን ሰላም ለመቀበል የተዘጋጀ ሰው ቢኖር ሰላማችሁ ከእርሱ ጋር ይኖራል። ካልሆነ ግን ሰላማችሁ ወደ እናንተ ይመለሳል።

decisions.choice: son of peace: a person who belongs to peace and is ready to welcome it
decisions.reason: "Son of" with a quality is a Hebrew way of describing someone marked by it ("sons of this age" and "sons of light", 16:8). Here it is someone open to the peace the messengers bring, who welcomes them (10:8).

decisions.choice: your peace will rest on him, or return to you: the blessing takes effect or comes back to the giver
alternatives: the messengers lose their peace if refused
decisions.reason: The greeting is pictured as a gift that settles on the one who receives it. If it is refused, it returns to the messengers, who lose nothing by it.

decisions.choice: a person of peace (B); someone ready to receive God's peace (R)
decisions.reason: "Son" here does not mean a male child; Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means. Readable spells out what being "of peace" means here.

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|él}}; la paz de ustedes | vuestra paz
decisions.reason: As in English: anyone, man or woman, may be the "son of peace" (meaning decision m1), and Spanish has both wordings, so the gender span mirrors the English one. With "ustedes", "su paz" could be read as that person's own peace; "la paz de ustedes" makes clear it is the messengers' greeting (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "sur lui" with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs {{gender:that person|him}}. In French "lui" refers back to "un fils de paix" (L) or to "quelqu'un" (B, R), a generic pronoun that already means anyone, so no span is needed (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: juu yake, naye, with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs a gender span for "that person" or "him". Swahili "juu yake" and "naye" serve for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "con của sự bình an" (L); "người yêu chuộng bình an" (B); "người sẵn lòng nhận sự bình an của Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says a person who belongs to peace and is ready to welcome it. Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable say who is meant, with no gender span, since "người" includes everyone.

decisions.choice: "평안의 아들" (L); "평안을 받을 만한 사람" (B); "하나님의 평안을 받아들일 사람" (R); no gender span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision). "그 사람" is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: uma pessoa de paz ... com ela (B); alguém ... com essa pessoa (R), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom "filho da paz" and puts "ele" under the setting, as the English does. Balanced and Readable say "uma pessoa" and "alguém", which already include men and women, so the pronoun that follows needs no setting.

decisions.choice: "የሰላም ልጅ" (child of peace, L); "በእርሱ" / "ከእርሱ ጋር" (with him), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span, as the English has for 'that person' or 'him'
decisions.reason: Amharic "ልጅ" means a child of either sex, and the masculine pronoun after "ሰው" (person) is the ordinary generic form that already includes women, so there are not two Amharic wordings for the setting to choose between. This holds for the generic pronouns through this passage (as 10:7).

source.text: ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένετε, ἐσθίοντες καὶ πίνοντες τὰ παρ’ αὐτῶν, ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: In the same now house remain, eating and drinking the things from them; worthy [is] for the worker of the wages of him.

en.L: And remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things [provided] by them, for the worker [is] worthy of {{gender:their|his}} wages.
en.B: Stay in that one house, eating and drinking whatever they give you, since a worker has earned {{gender:their|his}} pay.
en.R: Stay in that same house. Eat and drink what the people there give you. People who work should be paid for their work.

es.L: Y en esa misma casa {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}}, comiendo y bebiendo lo que ellos [den], porque digno [es] el trabajador de su salario.
es.B: {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} en esa misma casa, y {{plural_you:coman|comed}} y {{plural_you:beban|bebed}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} den, pues el trabajador se ha ganado su paga.
es.R: {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} en esa misma casa. {{plural_you:Coman|Comed}} y {{plural_you:beban|bebed}} lo que la gente de allí {{plural_you:les|os}} dé. Los que trabajan merecen que se les pague por su trabajo.

fr.L: Et demeurez dans cette même maison, mangeant et buvant ce qui [vient] d’eux, car l’ouvrier est digne de son salaire.
fr.B: Restez dans cette maison-là, et mangez et buvez ce qu’on vous donne, car un ouvrier a droit à son salaire.
fr.R: Restez dans cette même maison. Mangez et buvez ce que les gens de la maison vous donnent. Ceux qui travaillent doivent être payés pour leur travail.

sw.L: Na katika nyumba hiyo hiyo kaeni, mkila na kunywa vitu [vitolewavyo] nao; kwa maana mfanyakazi anastahili ujira wake.
sw.B: Kaeni katika nyumba hiyo hiyo, mkila na kunywa chochote watakachowapa, kwa maana mfanyakazi amestahili malipo yake.
sw.R: Kaeni katika nyumba hiyo hiyo. Kuleni na kunyweni kile ambacho watu wa huko watawapa. Watu wanaofanya kazi wanapaswa kulipwa kwa kazi yao.

vi.L: Và hãy ở lại trong chính nhà ấy, ăn và uống những gì họ [cho], vì người làm công đáng được tiền công của mình.
vi.B: Hãy ở lại trong nhà ấy, ăn uống những gì họ đãi các con, vì người làm công đáng được trả công.
vi.R: Hãy ở lại nhà đó. Hãy ăn uống những gì người ta cho các con. Người làm việc thì đáng được trả công.

ko.L: 그리고 그 집에 머물러, 그들이 주는 것을 먹고 마셔라. 일꾼이 자기 품삯을 받는 것은 마땅하기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 한 집에 머물면서, 그 집 사람들이 주는 것을 먹고 마셔라. 일꾼이 자기 품삯을 받는 것은 마땅하다.
ko.R: 그 집에서 지내라. 그 집 사람들이 주는 것을 먹고 마셔라. 일하는 사람은 일한 대가를 받아야 마땅하다.

pt.L: E fiquem nessa mesma casa, comendo e bebendo o que [lhes] derem, pois digno [é] o trabalhador do seu salário.
pt.B: Fiquem nessa casa, comendo e bebendo o que lhes oferecerem, porque quem trabalha merece o seu pagamento.
pt.R: Fiquem na mesma casa. Comam e bebam o que as pessoas dali derem a vocês. Quem trabalha deve receber pagamento pelo seu trabalho.

am.L: በዚያም ቤት ከእነርሱ ዘንድ [የሚቀርበውን] እየበላችሁና እየጠጣችሁ ቆዩ፤ ሠራተኛ ደመወዙ ይገባዋልና።
am.B: የሚሰጧችሁን እየበላችሁና እየጠጣችሁ በዚያው ቤት ቆዩ፤ ሠራተኛ ደመወዙን ሊያገኝ ይገባዋል።
am.R: በዚያው ቤት ቆዩ። የቤቱ ሰዎች የሚሰጧችሁን ብሉ፤ ጠጡም። የሚሠራ ሰው ለሥራው ሊከፈለው ይገባል።

decisions.choice: remain in the same house: the house where they were first welcomed
decisions.reason: As in 9:4, they are to keep the lodging where they are first received until they leave the town.

decisions.choice: the worker is worthy of his wages: a saying about fair pay
decisions.reason: The law told employers to pay a worker on the same day (Deuteronomy 24:14-15). Paul quotes this saying as Scripture (1 Timothy 5:18) and draws the same point for those who preach (1 Corinthians 9:14). Food and lodging are the messengers' pay.

decisions.choice: the things from them: what the household provides
decisions.reason: They eat what their hosts give them, as in 10:8.

decisions.choice: People who work should be paid for their work.
alternatives: the worker is worthy of his wages
decisions.reason: Readable puts the saying in plain words, with a plural that needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: el trabajador ... su salario, with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs a gender span for "their" or "his" wages; Spanish "su" serves for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "son salaire" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span on the possessive
decisions.reason: English writes {{gender:their|his}} wages. The French possessive "son" agrees with "salaire", not with the worker, so it says nothing about the worker's sex and needs no span.

decisions.choice: mfanyakazi ... ujira wake, with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs a gender span for "their" or "his" wages; Swahili "mfanyakazi" and "wake" serve for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "người làm công ... của mình" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 10:10: the Vietnamese words already include men and women, so the English span has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: o trabalhador do seu salário (L); quem trabalha merece o seu pagamento (B), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English puts "their/his" under the setting. The Portuguese possessive "seu" agrees with the wage, not the worker, so it says nothing about sex; Balanced and Readable say "quem trabalha", which means anyone, as Matthew 10:10 does.

decisions.choice: "ደመወዝ" (wages, pay)
decisions.reason: Here the Greek word means a worker's pay, so the Amharic says "ደመወዝ"; "ዋጋ" is kept for the reward God gives (Matthew 5:12; Luke 6:23).

source.text: μὴ μεταβαίνετε ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Not move from house to house.

en.L: Do not move from house to house.
en.B: Do not keep changing from one house to another.
en.R: Do not move around from one house to another.

es.L: No {{plural_you:se muden|os mudéis}} de casa en casa.
es.B: No {{plural_you:anden|andéis}} cambiando de una casa a otra.
es.R: No {{plural_you:se muden|os mudéis}} de una casa a otra.

fr.L: Ne passez pas de maison en maison.
fr.B: Ne changez pas sans cesse de maison.
fr.R: N’allez pas d’une maison à une autre.

sw.L: Msihame kutoka nyumba hadi nyumba.
sw.B: Msiwe mkihama kutoka nyumba moja kwenda nyingine.
sw.R: Msihamehame kutoka nyumba moja kwenda nyingine.

vi.L: Đừng dời từ nhà này sang nhà khác.
vi.B: Đừng cứ đổi từ nhà này sang nhà khác.
vi.R: Đừng dọn đi ở nhà này nhà nọ.

ko.L: 이 집에서 저 집으로 옮겨 다니지 마라.
ko.B: 이 집 저 집으로 자꾸 옮겨 다니지 마라.
ko.R: 이 집 저 집 옮겨 다니지 마라.

pt.L: Não passem de casa em casa.
pt.B: Não fiquem mudando de uma casa para outra.
pt.R: Não fiquem trocando de casa.

am.L: ከቤት ወደ ቤት አትዘዋወሩ።
am.B: ከአንዱ ቤት ወደ ሌላው ቤት አትቀያይሩ።
am.R: ከአንዱ ቤት ወደ ሌላው እየተዘዋወራችሁ አትኑሩ።

decisions.choice: do not move: do not make a habit of moving to other lodgings
decisions.reason: The present tense with the negative forbids a practice: leaving the first host for a better offer. They may still visit other homes to bring the message.

source.text: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν πόλιν εἰσέρχησθε καὶ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐσθίετε τὰ παρατιθέμενα ὑμῖν, καὶ θεραπεύετε τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἀσθενεῖς, καὶ λέγετε αὐτοῖς· Ἤγγικεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And into whatever city you might enter and they receive you, eat the things set before you, \v 9 and heal the in it sick, and say to them, Has come near upon you the kingdom of God.

en.L: And into whatever town you enter and they receive you, eat the things set before you, \v 9 and heal the sick in it, and say to them, 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'
en.B: Whenever a town takes you in, eat whatever food they put in front of you. \v 9 Heal those in it who are sick, and tell the people, 'The kingdom of God has drawn near to you.'
en.R: When you go into a town and the people welcome you, eat the food they give you. \v 9 Heal the sick people in that town. Tell them, 'The kingdom of God has come close to you.'

es.L: Y en cualquier ciudad en que {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} y {{plural_you:los|os}} reciban, {{plural_you:coman|comed}} lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} sirva, \v 9 y {{plural_you:sanen|sanad}} a los enfermos que haya en ella, y {{plural_you:díganles|decidles}}: “Se ha acercado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} el reino de Dios”.
es.B: Cuando un pueblo {{plural_you:los|os}} acoja, {{plural_you:coman|comed}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} pongan delante. \v 9 {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} a los enfermos que haya allí, y {{plural_you:digan|decid}} a la gente: “El reino de Dios se ha acercado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en un pueblo y la gente {{plural_you:los|os}} reciba bien, {{plural_you:coman|comed}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} den. \v 9 {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} a los enfermos de ese pueblo. {{plural_you:Díganles|Decidles}}: “El reino de Dios ya está muy cerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”.

fr.L: Et dans toute ville où vous entrerez et où l’on vous recevra, mangez ce qu’on met devant vous, \v 9 et guérissez les malades qui s’y trouvent, et dites-leur : “Le royaume de Dieu s’est approché de vous.”
fr.B: Quand une ville vous accueille, mangez ce qu’on vous sert. \v 9 Guérissez les malades qui s’y trouvent et dites aux gens : “Le royaume de Dieu est arrivé tout près de vous.”
fr.R: Quand vous entrez dans une ville et que les gens vous accueillent, mangez ce qu’ils vous donnent. \v 9 Guérissez les malades de cette ville. Dites-leur : “Le royaume de Dieu est venu tout près de vous.”

sw.L: Na mji wowote mtakaoingia nao wakawapokea, kuleni vitu vinavyowekwa mbele yenu, \v 9 na waponyeni wagonjwa walio ndani yake, na waambieni, 'Ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia kwenu.'
sw.B: Mkiingia katika mji wowote nao wakawakaribisha, kuleni chakula chochote watakachowaandalia. \v 9 Waponyeni wagonjwa waliomo, mkawaambie watu, 'Ufalme wa Mungu umewakaribia.'
sw.R: Mnapoingia katika mji na watu wakawakaribisha vizuri, kuleni chakula watakachowapa. \v 9 Waponyeni wagonjwa wa mji huo. Waambieni, 'Ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia sana kwenu.'

vi.L: Và vào thành nào mà người ta tiếp nhận các con, hãy ăn những gì được dọn ra cho các con, \v 9 và hãy chữa lành những người bệnh ở đó, và nói với họ: 'Vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đã đến gần các người.'
vi.B: Khi các con vào một thành nào và được người ta tiếp đón, hãy ăn những gì họ dọn cho các con. \v 9 Hãy chữa lành những người bệnh trong thành ấy và nói với họ: 'Vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đã đến gần các người.'
vi.R: Khi các con vào một thị trấn và người ta tiếp đón các con, hãy ăn những gì họ dọn cho các con. \v 9 Hãy chữa lành những người bệnh trong thị trấn ấy. Hãy nói với họ: 'Vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đã đến gần các người.'

ko.L: 그리고 어느 고을에 들어가든지 [사람들이] 너희를 맞아들이면, 너희 앞에 차려 놓은 것을 먹어라. \v 9 그리고 그 안에 있는 병자들을 고쳐 주고, 그들에게 '하나님의 나라가 너희에게 가까이 왔다' 하고 말하여라.
ko.B: 어느 고을에 들어가든지 그곳 사람들이 너희를 맞아들이면, 너희 앞에 차려 주는 음식을 먹어라. \v 9 그 고을의 병자들을 고쳐 주고, 사람들에게 '하나님의 나라가 너희에게 가까이 왔다' 하고 말하여라.
ko.R: 어떤 마을에 들어갔는데 사람들이 너희를 반겨 맞아 주면, 그들이 주는 음식을 먹어라. \v 9 그리고 그 마을의 아픈 사람들을 고쳐 주어라. 그 사람들에게 '하나님의 나라가 너희 가까이에 왔다' 하고 말하여라.

pt.L: E em qualquer cidade em que entrarem e [os] receberem, comam o que for posto diante de vocês, \v 9 e curem os doentes que nela [houver], e digam-lhes: 'O Reino de Deus se aproximou de vocês.'
pt.B: Quando uma cidade acolher vocês, comam o que puserem na frente de vocês. \v 9 Curem os doentes que houver ali e digam ao povo: 'O Reino de Deus chegou perto de vocês.'
pt.R: Quando vocês entrarem numa cidade e as pessoas receberem vocês bem, comam a comida que elas derem. \v 9 Curem os doentes daquela cidade. Digam a eles: 'O Reino de Deus está bem perto de vocês.'

am.L: ወደ ማንኛውም ከተማ ብትገቡና ቢቀበሏችሁ፣ የሚቀርብላችሁን ብሉ፤ \v 9 በእርሷም ያሉትን ድውዮች ፈውሱ፤ እንዲህም በሏቸው፦ “የእግዚአብሔር መንግሥት ወደ እናንተ ቀርባለች።”

decisions.choice: eat what is set before you: accept the hospitality offered
decisions.reason: They are not to be particular about their food but take what their hosts serve. Paul gives the same rule for eating with others (1 Corinthians 10:27).

decisions.choice: has come near: God's rule is close at hand and already at work
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw near. The healings show that God's rule is breaking in (11:20), though its full coming is still ahead (21:31).

decisions.choice: city: town
decisions.reason: The word is used for any town, however small (9:5).

decisions.choice: takes you in
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an everyday phrase for receiving guests.

decisions.choice: ciudad (L); pueblo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word covers any walled settlement, here the towns of Galilee and Judea (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "ciudad"; Balanced and Readable say "pueblo", the Spanish word for a town of this size, as the English says "town".

decisions.choice: le royaume de Dieu, every level (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form. "Règne" would bring out God's rule as an activity, but "royaume" is the word French readers know and keeps the phrase the same across the Gospels; the meaning decision explains that God's rule is at work.

decisions.choice: "các người" for the townspeople in the messengers' words (also 10:11)
decisions.reason: The messengers speak to a whole town as Jesus speaks to crowds; "đã đến gần" keeps the sense that God's rule is close at hand (meaning decision).

decisions.reason: Refusing the messengers is refusing Jesus, who sent them (10:16).

decisions.reason: As in Luke 9:5, 9:48 and Matthew 10:14.

records.literal_gloss: Even the dust that clung to us from the city of you on the feet we wipe off against you; yet this know, that has come near the kingdom of God.

en.L: 'Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet we wipe off against you. Yet know this, that the kingdom of God has come near.'
en.B: 'Against you we wipe off even the dust of your town that has stuck to our feet. All the same, be sure of this: the kingdom of God has come near.'
en.R: 'We are wiping even the dust of your town off our feet. It is a sign against you. But know this: the kingdom of God has come close.'

es.L: “Aun el polvo de {{plural_you:la ciudad de ustedes|vuestra ciudad}} que se nos ha pegado a los pies nos lo limpiamos contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; sin embargo, {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} esto: que se ha acercado el reino de Dios”.
es.B: “Contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} nos limpiamos hasta el polvo {{plural_you:del pueblo de ustedes|de vuestro pueblo}} que se nos ha pegado a los pies. Aun así, {{plural_you:estén|estad}} seguros de esto: el reino de Dios se ha acercado”.
es.R: “Nos sacudimos de los pies hasta el polvo {{plural_you:del pueblo de ustedes|de vuestro pueblo}}. Es una señal contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Pero {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} esto: el reino de Dios está cerca”.

fr.L: “Même la poussière de votre ville qui s’est collée à nos pieds, nous l’essuyons contre vous. Cependant, sachez ceci : le royaume de Dieu s’est approché.”
fr.B: “Nous essuyons contre vous jusqu’à la poussière de votre ville qui s’est collée à nos pieds. Mais sachez-le bien : le royaume de Dieu est arrivé tout près.”
fr.R: “Nous essuyons même la poussière de votre ville qui est restée sur nos pieds. C’est un signe contre vous. Mais sachez ceci : le royaume de Dieu est venu tout près.”

sw.L: 'Hata vumbi la mji wenu lililotushika miguuni tunalipangusa dhidi yenu. Lakini jueni hili, kwamba ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia.'
sw.B: 'Tunapangusa dhidi yenu hata vumbi la mji wenu lililoganda miguuni mwetu. Hata hivyo, jueni kwa hakika: ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia.'
sw.R: 'Tunapangusa hata vumbi la mji wenu kutoka miguuni mwetu. Ni ishara dhidi yenu. Lakini jueni hili: ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia.'

vi.L: 'Ngay cả bụi trong thành các người dính vào chân chúng tôi, chúng tôi cũng phủi đi nghịch lại các người; tuy vậy, hãy biết điều này: vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đã đến gần.'

vi.R: 'Chúng tôi phủi cả bụi của thị trấn các người khỏi chân mình. Đó là dấu hiệu để cảnh cáo các người. Nhưng hãy biết điều này: vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đã đến gần.'

ko.R: '우리는 발에 묻은 너희 마을의 먼지까지 털어 버린다. 이것은 너희에게 주는 경고이다. 그러나 하나님의 나라가 가까이 왔다는 것은 알아 두어라.'

pt.L: 'Até a poeira da cidade de vocês que se grudou aos nossos pés nós sacudimos contra vocês. Contudo, saibam isto: o Reino de Deus se aproximou.'

pt.R: 'Estamos limpando dos nossos pés até a poeira da cidade de vocês. Isso é um sinal contra vocês. Mas saibam disto: o Reino de Deus está bem perto.'

am.R: “በእግራችን ላይ የተጣበቀውን የከተማችሁን አቧራ እንኳ እናራግፋለን። ይህ በእናንተ ላይ ምልክት ነው። ነገር ግን ይህን እወቁ፤ የእግዚአብሔር መንግሥት ቀርባለች።”

decisions.choice: wiping off the dust: a public sign that the town is left to answer for itself
alternatives: a way of cleaning the feet
decisions.reason: The gesture says that the messengers take nothing of the town with them; they have done their part (9:5). Paul and Barnabas do it at Pisidian Antioch (Acts 13:51).

decisions.choice: against you: as evidence against you
decisions.reason: As in 9:5, the gesture is a witness that the town was told.

decisions.choice: yet know this: the kingdom comes near even to those who refuse it
alternatives: the kingdom has gone away from them
decisions.reason: The words to the welcoming town (10:9) are repeated without "to you". Refusing the message does not stop the kingdom from coming; the town will meet it as judgment (10:12).

decisions.choice: It is a sign against you.
decisions.reason: Readable makes "against you" its own sentence and says what the act means.

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" for the messengers speaking to the town
decisions.reason: The exclusive "chúng tôi" sets the messengers apart from the town they leave, which the sign of the dust does (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: The messengers speak to the town in 해라체 ("털어 버린다", "알아라")
decisions.reason: A public warning to a town that has turned them away, given as a declaration; it matches the plain style of Jesus' own words they are carrying.

decisions.choice: sacudimos (L, B); limpando (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to wipe off. Portuguese speaks of shaking off dust ("sacudir a poeira"), as Matthew 10:14 does; Readable says "limpar", the plain word for wiping the feet clean.

source.text: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι Σοδόμοις ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.

en.L: I say to you that on that day it will be more bearable for Sodom than for that town.
en.B: I tell you, on that day Sodom will be better off than that town.
en.R: I tell you, on the day God judges, things will go easier for Sodom than for that town.

es.L: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que en aquel día será más soportable para Sodoma que para aquella ciudad.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que en aquel día Sodoma saldrá mejor parada que ese pueblo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que el día en que Dios juzgue, a Sodoma le irá mejor que a ese pueblo.

fr.L: Je vous dis que, en ce jour-là, ce sera plus supportable pour Sodome que pour cette ville-là.
fr.B: Je vous le dis : ce jour-là, Sodome s’en tirera mieux que cette ville.
fr.R: Je vous le dis : le jour où Dieu jugera, cela ira moins mal pour Sodome que pour cette ville.

vi.B: Ta nói với các con, trong ngày ấy, Sô-đôm sẽ còn chịu hình phạt nhẹ hơn thành ấy.
vi.R: Ta nói với các con, vào ngày Đức Chúa Trời phán xét mọi người, thành Sô-đôm sẽ bị phạt nhẹ hơn thị trấn ấy.

ko.L: 내가 너희에게 말한다. 그날에는 소돔이 그 고을보다 더 견디기 쉬울 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 말한다. 그날에는 소돔이 그 고을보다 오히려 나을 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 너희에게 말한다. 하나님께서 심판하시는 날에, 소돔이 그 고을보다 벌을 덜 받을 것이다.

pt.L: Eu lhes digo que naquele dia será mais tolerável para Sodoma do que para aquela cidade.
pt.B: Eu lhes digo: naquele dia, Sodoma terá sorte melhor do que aquela cidade.
pt.R: Eu digo a vocês: no dia em que Deus julgar, vai ser mais fácil para Sodoma do que para aquela cidade.
