am.B: እላችኋለሁ፤ በዚያ ቀን ከዚያች ከተማ ይልቅ ለሰዶም ይሻላታል።
am.R: እላችኋለሁ፣ እግዚአብሔር በሚፈርድበት ቀን ከዚያች ከተማ ይልቅ ለሰዶም ይቀልላታል።

decisions.choice: Sodom: the city God destroyed for its wickedness
decisions.reason: Sodom was the standing example of a city ripe for judgment (Genesis 18:20; 19:24-25; Isaiah 1:9-10; Luke 17:28-29). Its men also mistreated the messengers God sent there (Genesis 19:1-11).

decisions.choice: that day: the day of judgment
alternatives: the day the town refuses them
decisions.reason: "That day" is the prophets' way of speaking of the day when God judges (Isaiah 2:11-12; Luke 17:31; 21:34). Verse 14 calls it "the judgment".

decisions.choice: more bearable: easier to endure, less severe
decisions.reason: Sodom will still be judged, but the town that heard the message and turned it away will fare worse.

decisions.choice: will be better off (B); things will go easier (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday wording for "more bearable".

decisions.choice: on the day God judges
decisions.reason: Readable says which day is meant.

decisions.choice: "Sô-đôm"; "chịu nhẹ hơn" (L), "chịu hình phạt nhẹ hơn" (B), "bị phạt nhẹ hơn" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 10:15: the Protestant transliteration, and "that day" is the day of judgment (meaning decision). This is a plain "I tell you", not "amen", so no "Thật vậy".

decisions.choice: "더 견디기 쉬울" (L), "오히려 나을" (B), "벌을 덜 받을" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the Korean Matthew 10:15 and 11:22-24, so the parallel sayings read alike.

decisions.choice: terá sorte melhor (B); vai ser mais fácil (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as Matthew 10:15 and 11:22-24, where the comparison is the same.

source.text: Οὐαί σοι, Χοραζίν· οὐαί σοι, Βηθσαϊδά· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν, πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ καθήμενοι μετενόησαν.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, Chorazin; woe to you, Bethsaida; because if in Tyre and Sidon had taken place the works of power that took place in you, long ago in sackcloth and ashes sitting they would have repented.

en.L: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the works of power that took place in you had taken place in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
en.B: How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the mighty deeds that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, their people would long ago have sat down in sackcloth and ashes and repented.
en.R: How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! Great miracles were done in your towns. If those miracles had been done in Tyre and Sidon, the people there would have turned away from their sins long ago. They would have sat in rough clothes and ashes to show how sorry they were.

es.L: ¡Ay de ti, Corazín! ¡Ay de ti, Betsaida! Porque si en Tiro y Sidón se hubieran hecho las obras poderosas que se hicieron en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, hace tiempo que se habrían arrepentido, sentados en saco y ceniza.
es.B: ¡Ay de ti, Corazín! ¡Ay de ti, Betsaida! Si las obras poderosas que se hicieron entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}} se hubieran hecho en Tiro y Sidón, hace mucho tiempo que sus habitantes se habrían vestido de saco, se habrían sentado en ceniza y se habrían arrepentido.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para ti, Corazín! ¡Qué terrible será para ti, Betsaida! En {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pueblos se hicieron grandes milagros. Si esos milagros se hubieran hecho en Tiro y Sidón, la gente de allí se habría apartado de sus pecados hace mucho tiempo. Se habrían sentado vestidos de ropa áspera y en ceniza, para mostrar cuánto lo lamentaban.

fr.L: Malheur à toi, Chorazin ! Malheur à toi, Bethsaïda ! Car si les actes de puissance qui ont eu lieu chez vous avaient eu lieu à Tyr et à Sidon, ils se seraient repentis depuis longtemps, assis dans le sac et la cendre.
fr.B: Malheur à toi, Chorazin ! Malheur à toi, Bethsaïda ! Si les miracles accomplis chez vous l’avaient été à Tyr et à Sidon, leurs habitants se seraient repentis depuis longtemps, vêtus de sacs et assis dans la cendre.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour toi, Chorazin ! Quel malheur pour toi, Bethsaïda ! De grands miracles ont été faits dans vos villes. Si ces miracles avaient été faits à Tyr et à Sidon, les gens de là-bas se seraient détournés de leurs péchés depuis longtemps. Ils se seraient assis dans des habits de toile grossière et dans la cendre pour montrer leur regret.

sw.L: Ole wako, Korazini! Ole wako, Bethsaida! Kwa maana kama matendo ya nguvu yaliyofanyika kwenu yangalifanyika katika Tiro na Sidoni, zamani sana wangalitubu, wakiketi katika magunia na majivu.
sw.B: Ole wako, Korazini! Ole wako, Bethsaida! Kama matendo ya nguvu yaliyofanyika kwenu yangefanyika katika Tiro na Sidoni, watu wa huko wangekuwa wametubu zamani sana, wakivaa magunia na kuketi katika majivu.
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya sana kwako, Korazini! Itakuwa vibaya sana kwako, Bethsaida! Miujiza mikubwa ilifanyika katika miji yenu. Kama miujiza hiyo ingefanyika katika Tiro na Sidoni, watu wa huko wangeziacha dhambi zao zamani sana. Wangeketi wakiwa wamevaa nguo za magunia na katika majivu, kuonyesha jinsi walivyojuta.

vi.L: Khốn cho ngươi, Cô-ra-xin! Khốn cho ngươi, Bết-sai-đa! Vì nếu các việc quyền năng đã làm giữa các ngươi được làm tại Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, thì họ đã ngồi trong áo vải gai và tro mà ăn năn từ lâu rồi.
vi.B: Khốn cho ngươi, Cô-ra-xin! Khốn cho ngươi, Bết-sai-đa! Nếu những việc quyền năng đã làm giữa các ngươi được làm tại Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, thì dân ở đó đã mặc áo vải gai, ngồi trong tro để tỏ lòng ăn năn từ lâu rồi.
vi.R: Thật khốn khổ cho ngươi, Cô-ra-xin! Thật khốn khổ cho ngươi, Bết-sai-đa! Nhiều phép lạ lớn đã được làm trong các thành của các ngươi. Nếu những phép lạ ấy được làm ở Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, thì dân ở đó đã từ bỏ tội lỗi từ lâu rồi. Họ đã mặc áo vải thô và ngồi trong tro để tỏ ra mình hối tiếc.

ko.L: 고라신아, 너에게 화가 있다! 벳새다야, 너에게 화가 있다! 너희에게서 일어난 능력 있는 일들이 두로와 시돈에서 일어났더라면, 그들은 벌써 오래전에 굵은 베옷을 입고 재 위에 앉아 회개하였을 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 고라신아, 너는 얼마나 불행하냐! 벳새다야, 너는 얼마나 불행하냐! 너희 가운데서 행한 능력 있는 일들을 두로와 시돈에서 행했더라면, 그곳 사람들은 벌써 오래전에 굵은 베옷을 입고 재 위에 앉아 회개하였을 것이다.
ko.R: 고라신아, 너에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! 벳새다야, 너에게도 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! 너희 마을에서 큰 기적들이 많이 일어났다. 그 기적들이 두로와 시돈에서 일어났더라면, 그곳 사람들은 벌써 오래전에 죄에서 돌이켰을 것이다. 그들은 거친 옷을 입고 재 위에 앉아서 자기들의 죄를 슬퍼했을 것이다.

pt.L: Ai de você, Corazim! Ai de você, Betsaida! Pois, se em Tiro e Sidom tivessem acontecido os feitos poderosos que aconteceram em vocês, há muito tempo elas teriam se arrependido, sentadas em pano de saco e cinza.
pt.B: Ai de você, Corazim! Ai de você, Betsaida! Se os feitos poderosos realizados entre vocês tivessem sido realizados em Tiro e Sidom, há muito tempo o povo de lá teria se sentado em pano de saco e cinza e se arrependido.
pt.R: Que coisa terrível vai acontecer com você, Corazim! Que coisa terrível com você, Betsaida! Grandes milagres foram feitos nas cidades de vocês. Se esses milagres tivessem sido feitos em Tiro e Sidom, as pessoas de lá teriam deixado os seus pecados há muito tempo. Elas teriam se sentado com roupas ásperas e na cinza para mostrar que estavam arrependidas.

am.L: ወዮልሽ ኮራዚን! ወዮልሽ ቤተ ሳይዳ! በእናንተ የተደረጉት የኃይል ሥራዎች በጢሮስና በሲዶና ተደርገው ቢሆን ኖሮ፣ ከብዙ ጊዜ በፊት በማቅና በአመድ ተቀምጠው ንስሓ በገቡ ነበርና።
am.B: ወዮልሽ ኮራዚን! ወዮልሽ ቤተ ሳይዳ! በእናንተ መካከል የተደረጉትን የኃይል ሥራዎች ጢሮስና ሲዶና አይተው ቢሆን ኖሮ፣ ሕዝባቸው ማቅ ለብሰውና በአመድ ላይ ተቀምጠው ከብዙ ጊዜ በፊት ንስሓ በገቡ ነበር።
am.R: ኮራዚን ሆይ፣ ክፉ ቀን ይጠብቅሻል! ቤተ ሳይዳ ሆይ፣ ክፉ ቀን ይጠብቅሻል! በከተሞቻችሁ ታላላቅ ተአምራት ተደርገዋል። እነዚህ ተአምራት በጢሮስና በሲዶና ተደርገው ቢሆን ኖሮ፣ በዚያ የሚኖሩት ሰዎች ከብዙ ጊዜ በፊት ከኃጢአታቸው በተመለሱ ነበር። ማዘናቸውን ለማሳየት ሻካራ ልብስ ለብሰው በአመድ ላይ በተቀመጡ ነበር።

decisions.choice: Chorazin and Bethsaida: towns near Capernaum, at the north end of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Jesus fed the five thousand near Bethsaida (9:10). Chorazin lay in the hills a short way north of Capernaum. The Gospels tell of no miracle in Chorazin; the saying shows that Jesus did more than they record (John 21:25).

decisions.choice: Tyre and Sidon: Gentile cities on the coast north of Galilee
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke against them for their pride and wealth (Isaiah 23; Ezekiel 26-28). Yet people from that coast came to hear Jesus (6:17).

decisions.choice: sitting in sackcloth and ashes: signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was rough cloth woven from goat's hair. People who mourned or repented wore it and sat in ashes, as the king of Nineveh did when Jonah preached (Jonah 3:6; Daniel 9:3).

decisions.choice: works of power: miracles
decisions.reason: The word means power, and in the plural, acts that show power (19:37; Acts 2:22).

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Woe" is rarely heard in everyday speech. Literal keeps the old cry; Balanced and Readable say what it means. The same wording as the woes of 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: turned away from their sins
decisions.reason: Readable explains repenting, as it does in 3:3 and 5:32.

decisions.choice: Great miracles were done in your towns. If those miracles had been done...
decisions.reason: Readable first states what happened, then the comparison.

decisions.choice: ¡Ay de ti! (L, B); ¡Qué terrible será para ti! (R)
decisions.reason: The word used across the New Testament drafts for this cry of grief and warning; Balanced keeps it, and Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does. "Obras poderosas" (L, B) and "milagros" (R) are likewise the drafts' words for these works of power (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the two towns, and "ciudad" is feminine, so the Peninsular form is "vosotras", as in Matthew 11:21. "Ti" for each town alone is singular and takes no span.

decisions.choice: Malheur à toi (L, B); Quel malheur pour toi (R)
alternatives: Quel malheur pour toi at Balanced too, as the English "How terrible for you"
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "Malheur à" at Literal and Balanced: unlike English "woe", it is still understood and used in French. Readable follows the English with an exclamation young readers hear as a lament. "Toi" because each town is addressed as one.

decisions.choice: se repentir (L, B); se détourner de leurs péchés (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms; Readable follows the English "turned away from their sins".

decisions.choice: Ole wako (L, B); Itakuwa vibaya sana kwako (R)
decisions.reason: The word used across the New Testament drafts for this cry of grief and warning; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: matendo ya nguvu (L, B); miujiza (R)
decisions.reason: The words used across the New Testament drafts for these works of power, which are miracles (meaning decision m4). "Kwenu" is plural, for the two towns together, and "wako" singular, for each alone.

decisions.choice: "ngươi", "các ngươi" for the towns (10:13-15)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Matthew 11:21-24: Jesus speaks to the towns themselves, as the prophets did in oracles of woe, and "ngươi" keeps them apart from the hearers he calls "các con".

decisions.choice: "Khốn cho" (L, B); "Thật khốn khổ cho" (R); "Cô-ra-xin", "Bết-sai-đa", "Ty-rơ", "Si-đôn"
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 11:21 and Luke 6:24-26, where "khốn cho" is the Bible's cry of grief and warning; the names in their Protestant forms.

decisions.choice: "너에게 화가 있다" (L), "너는 얼마나 불행하냐" (B), "끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다" (R); "능력 있는 일" (L, B), "기적" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Matthew 11:21, which has the same saying; the archaic "화 있을진저" is avoided (style guide, section 1).

decisions.choice: Ai de você (L, B); Que coisa terrível vai acontecer com você (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 11:21, the same saying: the cry is to each town, so "você", singular, though "vocês" follows for its people. Balanced keeps "Ai de", which Portuguese still uses, where the English Balanced changes the wording.

decisions.choice: The towns are addressed in the feminine singular ("ወዮልሽ", "ይጠብቅሻል")
decisions.reason: Amharic speaks of a town as "she", and the Greek addresses each town as "you" (singular), as in Matthew 11:21, whose wording this follows where the Greek is the same.

decisions.choice: "ክፉ ቀን ይጠብቅሻል" (a bad day awaits you) at Readable; "ወዮልሽ" at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: As the English Readable says "How terrible for you", the Readable Amharic says plainly what the cry of woe announces, as in Matthew 11:21.

source.text: πλὴν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν τῇ κρίσει ἢ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But for Tyre and Sidon more bearable it will be in the judgment than for you.

en.L: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
en.B: But at the judgment Tyre and Sidon will be better off than you.
en.R: When God judges, things will go easier for Tyre and Sidon than for you.

es.L: Sin embargo, para Tiro y Sidón será más soportable en el juicio que para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}.
es.B: Pero en el juicio Tiro y Sidón saldrán mejor libradas que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}.
es.R: Cuando Dios juzgue, a Tiro y Sidón les irá mejor que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}.

fr.L: Cependant, pour Tyr et Sidon, ce sera plus supportable lors du jugement que pour vous.
fr.B: Mais au jugement, Tyr et Sidon s’en tireront mieux que vous.
fr.R: Quand Dieu jugera, cela ira moins mal pour Tyr et Sidon que pour vous.

sw.L: Lakini kwa Tiro na Sidoni itavumilika zaidi katika hukumu kuliko kwenu.
sw.B: Lakini wakati wa hukumu Tiro na Sidoni zitapata nafuu kuliko ninyi.
sw.R: Mungu atakapohukumu, mambo yatakuwa rahisi zaidi kwa Tiro na Sidoni kuliko kwenu.

vi.L: Nhưng trong sự phán xét, Ty-rơ và Si-đôn sẽ được chịu nhẹ hơn các ngươi.
vi.B: Nhưng trong ngày phán xét, Ty-rơ và Si-đôn sẽ còn chịu nhẹ hơn các ngươi.
vi.R: Vào ngày Đức Chúa Trời phán xét, Ty-rơ và Si-đôn sẽ bị phạt nhẹ hơn các ngươi.

ko.L: 그러나 심판 때에는 두로와 시돈이 너희보다 더 견디기 쉬울 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 심판 때에는 두로와 시돈이 너희보다 오히려 나을 것이다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 심판하실 때에, 두로와 시돈이 너희보다 벌을 덜 받을 것이다.

pt.L: Contudo, para Tiro e Sidom será mais tolerável no juízo do que para vocês.
pt.B: Mas, no juízo, Tiro e Sidom terão sorte melhor do que vocês.
pt.R: Quando Deus julgar, vai ser mais fácil para Tiro e Sidom do que para vocês.

am.L: ነገር ግን በፍርዱ ከእናንተ ይልቅ ለጢሮስና ለሲዶና ይቀልላቸዋል።
am.B: ነገር ግን በፍርድ ቀን ከእናንተ ይልቅ ለጢሮስና ለሲዶና ይሻላቸዋል።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር በሚፈርድበት ጊዜ ከእናንተ ይልቅ ለጢሮስና ለሲዶና ይቀልላቸዋል።

decisions.choice: the judgment: God's final judgment
decisions.reason: This is the day of 10:12. Those who saw and heard Jesus will be judged by what they were shown (11:31-32; 12:48).

decisions.choice: than for you: the people of Chorazin and Bethsaida
decisions.reason: Jesus still speaks to the towns of 10:13, as if they were present.

decisions.choice: will be better off (B); things will go easier (R)
decisions.reason: As in 10:12.

decisions.choice: When God judges
decisions.reason: Readable says who judges.

source.text: καὶ σύ, Καφαρναούμ, μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ;

records.literal_gloss: And you, Capernaum, not to heaven will you be lifted up?

en.L: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven?
en.B: And you, Capernaum, will you be raised as high as heaven?
en.R: And you, people of Capernaum, do you think you will be lifted up to heaven?

es.L: Y tú, Cafarnaúm, ¿acaso hasta [el] cielo serás elevada?
es.B: Y tú, Cafarnaúm, ¿serás alzada tan alto como el cielo?
es.R: Y tú, pueblo de Cafarnaúm, ¿crees que serás elevado hasta el cielo?

fr.L: Et toi, Capharnaüm, seras-tu élevée jusqu’au ciel ?
fr.B: Et toi, Capharnaüm, vas-tu être élevée aussi haut que le ciel ?
fr.R: Et vous, les habitants de Capharnaüm, pensez-vous que vous serez élevés jusqu’au ciel ?

sw.L: Na wewe, Kapernaumu, je, hadi mbinguni utainuliwa?
sw.B: Na wewe, Kapernaumu, je, utapandishwa juu hadi mbinguni?
sw.R: Nanyi, watu wa Kapernaumu, je, mnadhani mtainuliwa hadi mbinguni?

vi.L: Còn ngươi, Ca-bê-na-um, ngươi sẽ được nâng lên đến tận trời sao?
vi.B: Còn ngươi, Ca-bê-na-um, ngươi tưởng sẽ được tôn cao đến tận trời sao?
vi.R: Còn dân thành Ca-bê-na-um, các ngươi nghĩ mình sẽ được nâng lên đến tận trời sao?

ko.L: 그리고 너 가버나움아, 네가 하늘까지 높아지겠느냐?
ko.B: 그리고 너 가버나움아, 네가 하늘까지 높아질 것 같으냐?
ko.R: 그리고 가버나움 사람들아! 너희는 너희가 하늘까지 높아질 것이라고 생각하느냐?

pt.L: E você, Cafarnaum, por acaso será elevada até o céu?
pt.B: E você, Cafarnaum, será erguida até o céu?
pt.R: E vocês, moradores de Cafarnaum, acham que vão ser levantados até o céu?

am.L: አንቺም ቅፍርናሆም፣ እስከ ሰማይ ከፍ ትደረጊያለሽን?
am.B: አንቺም ቅፍርናሆም፣ እስከ ሰማይ ድረስ ትከበሪያለሽን?
am.R: እናንተም የቅፍርናሆም ሰዎች፣ እስከ ሰማይ ከፍ የምትደረጉ ይመስላችኋል?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
alternatives: a statement: you will be lifted up
decisions.reason: The Greek question is worded to expect "No". Capernaum had been Jesus's base (4:31; 7:1) and had seen much of his work, and it may have thought itself raised high by it.

decisions.choice: will you be lifted up to heaven? (SBLGNT)
alternatives: you who have been lifted up to heaven
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a statement about the town instead of a question; the question has strong early support. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: lifted up to heaven: echoing Isaiah 14:13
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the king of Babylon says in his heart that he will climb up to heaven (Isaiah 14:13). The next sentence finishes the echo.

decisions.choice: people of Capernaum; do you think
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the town means its people and that the question challenges what they think of themselves.

decisions.choice: tú, pueblo de Cafarnaúm
decisions.reason: The English Readable speaks to the people of the town (rendering decision r-en-1). Spanish "pueblo" means both the town and its people, so Readable can say that while keeping the singular "tú" of the Greek.

decisions.choice: vous, les habitants de Capharnaüm (R)
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the people of the town, as the English does, so French uses "vous" for them; Literal and Balanced keep "toi" for the town, which is feminine in French ("élevée").

decisions.choice: Nanyi, watu wa Kapernaumu ... mnadhani
decisions.reason: The English Readable speaks to the people of the town (rendering decision r-en-1). Swahili verbs must then be plural, so Readable uses "ninyi" here and in the next sentence; Literal and Balanced keep the singular of the Greek.

decisions.choice: por acaso
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 11:23: the question expects the answer no (m1), and Portuguese marks that with "por acaso".

source.text: ἕως τοῦ ᾅδου καταβιβασθήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: To Hades you will be brought down.

en.L: To Hades you will be brought down.
en.B: No, you will be brought down to Hades.
en.R: No, God will bring you down to the place of the dead.

es.L: Hasta el Hades serás abatida.
es.B: No, serás abatida hasta el Hades.
es.R: No, Dios te hará bajar al lugar de los muertos.

fr.L: Jusqu’à l’Hadès tu seras abaissée.
fr.B: Non, tu seras précipitée jusqu’au séjour des morts.
fr.R: Non, Dieu vous fera descendre jusqu’au séjour des morts.

sw.L: Hadi Kuzimu utashushwa.
sw.B: Hapana, utashushwa hadi Kuzimu.
sw.R: Hapana, Mungu atawashusha mpaka Kuzimu, mahali pa wafu.

vi.L: Ngươi sẽ bị đem xuống tận Ha-đét.
vi.B: Không, ngươi sẽ bị đày xuống âm phủ.
vi.R: Không đâu, Đức Chúa Trời sẽ đày các ngươi xuống nơi của người chết.

ko.L: 너는 하데스까지 끌어내려질 것이다.
ko.B: 아니다. 너는 죽은 사람들의 세계까지 끌어내려질 것이다.
ko.R: 아니다. 하나님께서 너희를 죽은 사람들이 가는 곳까지 끌어내리실 것이다.

pt.L: Até o Hades você será derrubada.
pt.B: Não, você será derrubada até o mundo dos mortos.
pt.R: Não, Deus vai derrubar vocês até o mundo dos mortos.

am.L: እስከ ሲኦል ዝቅ ትደረጊያለሽ።
am.B: አይደለም፣ እስከ ሲኦል ድረስ ዝቅ ትደረጊያለሽ።
am.R: አይደለም፣ እግዚአብሔር ሙታን ወዳሉበት ስፍራ ያወርዳችኋል።

decisions.choice: Hades: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses the word for Sheol, the world of the dead below the earth (Psalm 16:10; Acts 2:27). Here it is the opposite of heaven: the lowest place, a picture of utter humbling under judgment.

decisions.choice: brought down to Hades: echoing Isaiah 14:15
decisions.reason: Isaiah tells the king of Babylon, who wanted to climb to heaven, that he will be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit (Isaiah 14:13-15). The proud town will share that fate.

decisions.choice: you will be brought down (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have the passive "you will be brought down", the wording of the Greek of Isaiah 14:15; some early ones, among them Papyrus 75 and Codex Vaticanus, have "you will go down". The meaning is much the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: No,
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable answer the question of the previous sentence.

decisions.choice: God will bring you down to the place of the dead
alternatives: you will be brought down to Hades
decisions.reason: Readable explains Hades and names God as the one who brings the town down, which the passive implies.

decisions.choice: el Hades (L, B); el lugar de los muertos (R)
decisions.reason: The word used across the New Testament drafts for the place of the dead (meaning decision m1); "infierno" is kept for Gehenna. Readable says what it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: l’Hadès (L); le séjour des morts (B, R)
alternatives: l’Hadès at Balanced, as the English
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms. "Le séjour des morts" is the established French phrase for the place of the dead, so Balanced can use it where the English keeps the name; "l'enfer" would suggest a place of punishment, which the word does not say here.

decisions.choice: Kuzimu, at every level
decisions.reason: The word used across the New Testament drafts for the place of the dead (meaning decision m1); "jehanamu" is kept for Gehenna. Readable adds "mahali pa wafu" to say what it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Ha-đét" (L); "âm phủ" (B); "nơi của người chết" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Matthew 11:23: Hades is the place of the dead (meaning decision), not Gehenna, which is "địa ngục".

decisions.choice: "하데스" (L); "죽은 사람들의 세계" (B); "죽은 사람들이 가는 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: Hades is worded as in the Korean Matthew 11:23 and 16:18: Literal keeps the name, Balanced and Readable say what it is, the realm of the dead (meaning decision). "음부" is the wording of older Korean Bibles and no longer understood.

decisions.choice: vocês
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the people of Capernaum, as its previous sentence does, so the pronoun is plural; Literal and Balanced speak to the town, "você", feminine like "cidade".

decisions.choice: "ዝቅ ትደረጊያለሽ" (you will be brought low), the passive
decisions.reason: Luke has the passive "you will be brought down", answering "ከፍ ትደረጊያለሽ" (you will be lifted up) in 10:15, where Matthew 11:23 has "you will go down"; the Amharic follows the Greek difference.

decisions.choice: "ሲኦል" at Literal and Balanced; "ሙታን ወዳሉበት ስፍራ" (the place where the dead are) at Readable
decisions.reason: Hades is the place of the dead, not Gehenna, the place of punishment, so the Amharic keeps "ሲኦል" and does not say "ገሃነም"; Readable explains it, as in Matthew 11:23.

source.text: Ὁ ἀκούων ὑμῶν ἐμοῦ ἀκούει, καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ ἀθετεῖ· ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ ἀθετῶν ἀθετεῖ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.

records.literal_gloss: The one hearing you me hears, and the one rejecting you me rejects; and the one me rejecting rejects the one having sent me.

en.L: The one who hears you hears {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who rejects you rejects {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and the one who rejects {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejects the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Anyone who listens to you listens to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Anyone who turns you away turns {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} away, and anyone who turns {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} away turns away the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: When people listen to you, they are listening to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. When people turn you away, they are turning {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} away. And anyone who turns {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} away is turning away God, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: El que {{plural_you:los|os}} oye, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} oye; y el que {{plural_you:los|os}} rechaza, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rechaza; y el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rechaza, rechaza al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».
es.B: El que {{plural_you:los|os}} escucha, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} escucha a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. El que {{plural_you:los|os}} rechaza, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rechaza a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rechaza, rechaza al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».
es.R: Cuando la gente {{plural_you:los|os}} escucha, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} está escuchando a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Cuando la gente {{plural_you:los|os}} rechaza, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} está rechazando a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rechaza está rechazando a Dios, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».

fr.L: Celui qui vous écoute {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écoute, et celui qui vous rejette {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejette ; et celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejette rejette celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »
fr.B: Qui vous écoute {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écoute. Qui vous repousse {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} repousse, et qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} repousse repousse celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »
fr.R: Quand les gens vous écoutent, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’ils écoutent. Quand les gens vous refusent, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’ils refusent. Et celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} refuse, c’est Dieu qu’il refuse, Dieu qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »

sw.L: Anayewasikiliza ninyi ananisikiliza {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, na anayewakataa ninyi ananikataa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}; na anayenikataa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} anamkataa yule aliyenituma."
sw.B: Yeyote anayewasikiliza ninyi ananisikiliza {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Yeyote anayewakataa ninyi ananikataa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, na yeyote anayenikataa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} anamkataa yule aliyenituma."
sw.R: Watu wanapowasikiliza ninyi, wananisikiliza {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Watu wanapowakataa ninyi, wananikataa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Na yeyote anayenikataa anamkataa Mungu, aliyenituma."

vi.L: Ai nghe các con là nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và ai khước từ các con là khước từ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; còn ai khước từ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là khước từ Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Ai nghe các con là nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ai khước từ các con là khước từ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và ai khước từ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là khước từ Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Khi người ta nghe các con, là họ nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Khi người ta từ chối các con, là họ từ chối {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Còn ai từ chối {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là từ chối Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 너희 말을 듣는 사람은 내 말을 듣는 것이고, 너희를 저버리는 사람은 나를 저버리는 것이다. 그리고 나를 저버리는 사람은 나를 보내신 분을 저버리는 것이다."
ko.B: 너희 말을 듣는 사람은 내 말을 듣는 것이다. 너희를 거절하는 사람은 나를 거절하는 것이고, 나를 거절하는 사람은 나를 보내신 분을 거절하는 것이다."
ko.R: 사람들이 너희 말을 들으면, 그것은 내 말을 듣는 것이다. 사람들이 너희를 받아들이지 않으면, 그것은 나를 받아들이지 않는 것이다. 그리고 나를 받아들이지 않는 사람은 나를 보내신 하나님을 받아들이지 않는 것이다."

pt.L: Quem ouve vocês ouve a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e quem rejeita vocês rejeita a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}; e quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejeita rejeita aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou."
pt.B: Quem escuta vocês escuta a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Quem recusa vocês recusa a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recusa recusa aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou."
pt.R: Quando as pessoas escutam vocês, estão escutando a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Quando mandam vocês embora, estão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mandando embora. E quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} manda embora está mandando embora Deus, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou."

am.L: እናንተን የሚሰማ እኔን ይሰማል፤ እናንተን የሚንቅም እኔን ይንቃል፤ እኔን የሚንቅም የላከኝን ይንቃል።»
am.B: እናንተን የሚሰማ ሁሉ እኔን ይሰማል። እናንተን የሚገፋ እኔን ይገፋል፤ እኔን የሚገፋ ደግሞ የላከኝን ይገፋል።»
am.R: ሰዎች እናንተን ሲሰሙ እኔን መስማታቸው ነው። እናንተን ሲገፉ እኔን መግፋታቸው ነው። እኔን የሚገፋ ደግሞ የላከኝን እግዚአብሔርን ይገፋል።»

decisions.choice: hearing you is hearing me: the messengers speak for Jesus
alternatives: the messengers speak only for themselves
decisions.reason: A messenger stood for the one who sent him. To welcome or refuse Jesus's messengers is to welcome or refuse him (9:48; John 13:20).

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God
decisions.reason: Jesus himself was sent by God (4:18, 43; 9:48).

decisions.choice: reject: refuse, set aside as worthless
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat as void or refuse to accept, as the Pharisees refused God's purpose (7:30).

decisions.choice: turns away
decisions.reason: An everyday phrase for refusing someone.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names the sender.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} after the verb
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "me" first for weight. Swahili carries "me" in the verb ("ananisikiliza") and repeats the free pronoun "mimi" for the same weight; as a pronoun for Jesus it takes the setting.

decisions.choice: "khước từ" (L, B); "từ chối" (R) for reject
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says refuse, set aside as worthless; "khước từ" is a firm refusal of a person or an offer, and Readable uses the everyday "từ chối".

decisions.choice: recusa (B); manda embora (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: everyday words for refusing someone. Literal keeps "rejeitar".

decisions.choice: "የሚንቅ" (who sets aside, despises) at Literal; "የሚገፋ" (who pushes away, rejects) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to set aside as worthless; Literal keeps that with "መናቅ", while Balanced and Readable use "መግፋት", the everyday Amharic way of saying that someone turns a person away.

source.text: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα δύο μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες· Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου.

records.literal_gloss: Returned then the seventy-two with joy saying, Lord, even the demons are subject to us in the name of you.

en.L: And the seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons submit to us in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name!"
en.B: The seventy-two came back full of joy. "Lord," they said, "when we use {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, even the demons obey us!"
en.R: Later the seventy-two followers came back filled with joy. They said, "Lord, even the demons obey us when we use {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name!"

es.L: Y volvieron los setenta y dos con alegría, diciendo: «Señor, aun los demonios se nos someten en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre».
es.B: Los setenta y dos volvieron llenos de alegría. «Señor —dijeron—, cuando usamos {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre, ¡hasta los demonios nos obedecen!».
es.R: Más tarde, los setenta y dos discípulos volvieron muy alegres. Dijeron: «Señor, ¡hasta los demonios nos obedecen cuando usamos {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre!».

fr.L: Et les soixante-douze revinrent avec joie, disant : « Seigneur, même les démons nous sont soumis en {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ! »
fr.B: Les soixante-douze revinrent pleins de joie. « Seigneur, dirent-ils, quand nous agissons en {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom, même les démons nous obéissent ! »
fr.R: Plus tard, les soixante-douze disciples sont revenus, remplis de joie. Ils ont dit : « Seigneur, même les démons nous obéissent quand nous utilisons {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ! »

sw.L: Basi wale sabini na wawili wakarudi kwa furaha, wakisema, "Bwana, hata pepo wanatutii kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}!"
sw.B: Wale sabini na wawili walirudi wakiwa wamejaa furaha. Wakasema, "Bwana, tunapotumia jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}, hata pepo wanatutii!"
sw.R: Baadaye wale wanafunzi sabini na wawili walirudi wakiwa na furaha kubwa. Walisema, "Bwana, hata pepo wanatutii tunapotumia jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}!"

vi.L: Bảy mươi hai người trở về cách vui mừng, nói: "Lạy Chúa, nhờ danh Chúa, ngay cả các quỷ cũng phục chúng con!"
vi.B: Bảy mươi hai người trở về, lòng đầy vui mừng, thưa: "Lạy Chúa, khi chúng con nhân danh Chúa, ngay cả các quỷ cũng vâng phục chúng con!"
vi.R: Sau đó, bảy mươi hai môn đồ trở về, lòng tràn đầy vui mừng. Họ thưa: "Lạy Chúa, khi chúng con dùng danh Chúa, ngay cả các quỷ cũng vâng lời chúng con!"

ko.L: 그리고 일흔두 사람이 기뻐하며 돌아와서 말했다. "주님, 주님의 이름으로 귀신들까지도 저희에게 복종합니다!"
ko.B: 일흔두 사람이 기쁨에 넘쳐 돌아와서 말했다. "주님, 저희가 주님의 이름을 쓰면 귀신들까지도 저희에게 복종합니다!"
ko.R: 얼마 뒤에 일흔두 사람이 아주 기뻐하며 돌아왔다. 그들이 말했다. "주님, 저희가 주님의 이름을 쓰면 귀신들까지도 저희 말을 듣습니다!"

pt.L: E os setenta e dois voltaram com alegria, dizendo: "Senhor, até os demônios se submetem a nós no {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome!"
pt.B: Os setenta e dois voltaram cheios de alegria. "Senhor", disseram eles, "quando usamos o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome, até os demônios nos obedecem!"
pt.R: Mais tarde, os setenta e dois seguidores voltaram muito alegres. Eles disseram: "Senhor, até os demônios nos obedecem quando usamos o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome!"

am.L: ሰባ ሁለቱም፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ አጋንንት እንኳ በስምህ ይገዙልናል!» እያሉ በደስታ ተመለሱ።
am.B: ሰባ ሁለቱም ደስታ ተሞልተው ተመለሱና፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ ስምህን ስንጠራ አጋንንት እንኳ ይታዘዙልናል!» አሉ።

decisions.choice: seventy-two (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The same variant as in 10:1, with the manuscripts divided in the same way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: submit: are made subject, obey
decisions.reason: The verb means to be placed under someone's authority. The demons had to do what they were told.

decisions.choice: in your name: by your authority, calling on your name
decisions.reason: They drove out demons by commanding them in Jesus's name (9:49; Acts 16:18).

decisions.choice: even: more than they expected
decisions.reason: They had been told to heal the sick (10:9); power over demons is more than they were promised.

decisions.choice: Later; followers
decisions.reason: Readable marks the passing of time and says who the seventy-two were.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa", "Chúa" for "you" and "chúng con" for themselves, with no setting span
decisions.reason: As in Luke 9:54: disciples who call Jesus "Lord" say "Lạy Chúa", the form settled for the Gospels; words of address take no span.

decisions.choice: "주님" for kyrie, and "주님의 이름" for "your name"
decisions.reason: The address as settled for the Korean Gospels; Korean repeats the title instead of using a pronoun for Jesus.

en.B: He told them, "I watched Satan fall from heaven like a flash of lightning.
en.R: Jesus answered, "I saw Satan fall from heaven as fast as lightning.

vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Ta đã thấy Sa-tan từ trời rơi xuống nhanh như tia chớp.

ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "나는 사탄이 번개처럼 빠르게 하늘에서 떨어지는 것을 보았다.

am.L: እርሱም እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «ሰይጣን እንደ መብረቅ ከሰማይ ሲወድቅ እመለከት ነበር።
am.B: እርሱም እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «ሰይጣን እንደ መብረቅ ብልጭታ ከሰማይ ሲወድቅ አየሁ።
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ሲል መለሰላቸው፦ «ሰይጣን እንደ መብረቅ ፈጥኖ ከሰማይ ሲወድቅ አየሁ።

decisions.choice: I was watching: Jesus saw it while the seventy-two were at work
alternatives: a vision of the end of time
decisions.reason: The past continuous tense describes what Jesus was seeing. The power of the seventy-two over demons showed that Satan's rule was being broken. Luke does not say whether it was a vision.

decisions.choice: fall from heaven: possibly echoing Isaiah 14:12
decisions.reason: Isaiah pictures the proud king of Babylon as the morning star fallen from heaven (Isaiah 14:12). Jesus uses a like picture for Satan's sudden defeat. Lightning is swift and seen by all.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary, the devil
decisions.reason: The name means "adversary" or "accuser" in Hebrew (Job 1:6). Luke also calls him the devil (4:2).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: as fast as lightning
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture points to: the fall was sudden.

decisions.choice: "Sa-tan"
decisions.reason: The name, as in Mark 1:13 and John 13:27; "ma quỷ" is kept for the word "devil" (Luke 4:2).

decisions.choice: "đã thấy" (L) for the imperfect "was watching"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says Jesus saw it while the seventy-two were at work; Vietnamese "đã thấy" places the seeing in that time, where "đang nhìn" would sound as if it were happening now.

decisions.choice: "사탄" for satanas
decisions.reason: "사탄" for satanas and "마귀" for diabolos, as settled for the Korean Luke and Matthew.

decisions.choice: Eu via Satanás caindo
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the past continuous of m1 with the imperfect "via" and the gerund; Balanced and Readable say "vi ... cair", as the English does.

source.text: ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ, καὶ οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς οὐ μὴ ἀδικήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Behold I have given you the authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and upon all the power of the enemy, and nothing you not not will harm.

en.L: Look, I have given you the authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you in any way.
en.B: I have given you authority to trample snakes and scorpions underfoot, and authority over all the enemy's power. Nothing at all will be able to hurt you.
en.R: I have given you power to step on snakes and scorpions. I have given you power over everything the enemy can do. Nothing will hurt you at all.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado la autoridad de pisar sobre serpientes y escorpiones, y sobre todo el poder del enemigo, y nada {{plural_you:les|os}} hará daño de ningún modo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dado autoridad para pisotear serpientes y escorpiones, y autoridad sobre todo el poder del enemigo. Nada en absoluto podrá {{plural_you:hacerles|haceros}} daño.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dado poder para pisar serpientes y escorpiones. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dado poder sobre todo lo que el enemigo puede hacer. Nada {{plural_you:les|os}} hará daño.

fr.L: Voici, je vous ai donné l’autorité de marcher sur les serpents et les scorpions, et sur toute la puissance de l’ennemi, et rien ne vous nuira en aucune façon.
fr.B: Je vous ai donné autorité pour écraser sous vos pieds serpents et scorpions, et autorité sur toute la puissance de l’ennemi. Rien ne pourra vous faire le moindre mal.
fr.R: Je vous ai donné le pouvoir de marcher sur les serpents et les scorpions. Je vous ai donné le pouvoir sur tout ce que l’ennemi peut faire. Rien ne vous fera de mal, rien du tout.

sw.L: Tazameni, nimewapa mamlaka ya kukanyaga juu ya nyoka na nge, na juu ya nguvu zote za adui, wala hakuna kitu kitakachowadhuru kamwe.
sw.B: Nimewapa mamlaka ya kuwakanyaga nyoka na nge, na mamlaka juu ya nguvu zote za adui. Hakuna kitu chochote kitakachoweza kuwadhuru.
sw.R: Nimewapa uwezo wa kuwakanyaga nyoka na nge. Nimewapa uwezo juu ya kila kitu ambacho adui anaweza kufanya. Hakuna kitu kitakachowadhuru hata kidogo.

vi.L: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho các con thẩm quyền để giày đạp trên rắn và bò cạp, và trên mọi quyền lực của kẻ thù, và không gì có thể làm hại các con được.

vi.R: Ta đã ban cho các con quyền để đạp lên rắn và bò cạp. Ta đã ban cho các con quyền trên mọi sức mạnh của kẻ thù. Không gì làm hại các con được.

ko.L: 보라, 내가 너희에게 뱀과 전갈을 밟고, 원수의 모든 능력을 [이기는] 권위를 주었다. 그리고 어떤 것도 결코 너희를 해치지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 뱀과 전갈을 짓밟고 원수의 모든 힘을 누를 권위를 주었다. 그러니 그 무엇도 너희를 결코 해치지 못할 것이다.

am.L: እነሆ፣ እባቦችንና ጊንጦችን ልትረግጡ፣ በጠላትም ኃይል ሁሉ ላይ ሥልጣንን ሰጥቻችኋለሁ፤ ምንም ነገር ፈጽሞ አይጎዳችሁም።
am.B: እባቦችንና ጊንጦችን እንድትረግጡ፣ በጠላትም ኃይል ሁሉ ላይ ሥልጣን ሰጥቻችኋለሁ። ምንም ነገር በምንም መንገድ ሊጎዳችሁ አይችልም።
am.R: እባቦችንና ጊንጦችን እንድትረግጡ ኃይል ሰጥቻችኋለሁ። ጠላት በሚያደርገው ነገር ሁሉ ላይ ኃይል ሰጥቻችኋለሁ። ምንም ነገር አይጎዳችሁም።

decisions.choice: tread on snakes and scorpions: recalling Psalm 91:13 and Deuteronomy 8:15
alternatives: only a promise of safety from real animals
decisions.reason: God promises the one who trusts in him that he will tread on the lion and the serpent (Psalm 91:13). Snakes and scorpions were dangers of the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:15). They stand for the powers of evil as well as for real danger (Acts 28:3-6).

decisions.choice: the enemy: Satan
decisions.reason: Satan has just been named (10:18). He is the enemy of God and of God's people (Matthew 13:39).

decisions.choice: nothing will harm you at all: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek piles up negatives for emphasis. It promises that the enemy cannot defeat them, not that they will never suffer; Jesus later warns that some will be put to death, yet not a hair of their head will perish (21:16-18).

decisions.choice: I have given: a gift that stands
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means the authority has been given and remains theirs.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: power (for both words)
decisions.reason: Readable uses "power" for both the right to act and the strength to act, since the difference is hard to put simply.

decisions.choice: "thẩm quyền" and "quyền lực" kept apart (L, B); "quyền" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has two words, authority and power, as in Luke 9:1; Readable uses one plain word for both, as the English Readable does. "kẻ thù" is Satan (meaning decision), lowercase as in the English.

records.literal_gloss: Yet in this not rejoice, that the spirits to you are subject, rejoice however that the names of you have been written in the heavens.

en.L: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens."
en.B: But do not be glad because the spirits obey you. Be glad instead that your names stand written in heaven."
en.R: But do not be happy because the spirits obey you. Be happy because your names are written in heaven."

es.L: Sin embargo, no {{plural_you:se alegren|os alegréis}} de esto, de que los espíritus se {{plural_you:les|os}} someten, sino {{plural_you:alégrense|alegraos}} de que {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} nombres han sido escritos en los cielos».

fr.L: Cependant, ne vous réjouissez pas de ceci, que les esprits vous sont soumis, mais réjouissez-vous de ce que vos noms ont été inscrits dans les cieux. »
fr.B: Pourtant, ne vous réjouissez pas de ce que les esprits vous obéissent ; réjouissez-vous plutôt de ce que vos noms sont inscrits dans le ciel. »
fr.R: Mais ne soyez pas heureux parce que les esprits vous obéissent. Soyez heureux parce que vos noms sont écrits dans le ciel. »

vi.R: Nhưng đừng vui vì các tà linh vâng lời các con. Hãy vui vì tên các con đã được ghi trên trời."

ko.L: 그러나 영들이 너희에게 복종한다는 이것으로 기뻐하지 말고, 너희 이름이 하늘에 기록되어 있다는 것으로 기뻐하여라."
ko.B: 그러나 영들이 너희에게 복종한다고 해서 기뻐하지 말고, 너희 이름이 하늘에 적혀 있는 것을 기뻐하여라."
ko.R: 그러나 악한 영들이 너희 말을 듣는다고 기뻐하지 마라. 너희 이름이 하늘에 적혀 있으니, 그것을 기뻐하여라."

pt.L: Contudo, não se alegrem com isto, que os espíritos se submetem a vocês; alegrem-se, porém, porque os nomes de vocês estão escritos nos céus."
pt.B: Mas não fiquem contentes porque os espíritos obedecem a vocês. Fiquem contentes, isso sim, porque os nomes de vocês estão escritos no céu."
pt.R: Mas não fiquem felizes porque os espíritos obedecem a vocês. Fiquem felizes porque os nomes de vocês estão escritos no céu."
